tEn: Cerebras Systems Inc. — Form 424B4 Final Prospectus (IPO)
tZh: Cerebras Systems Inc. —424B4 最终招股说明书（IPO）
sEn: Cerebras Systems' IPO prospectus pitches its Wafer-Scale Engine as the world's fastest AI inference infrastructure, citing 15x faster inference than GPU-based solutions, revenue growth from $24.6 million in 2022 to $510.0 million in 2025, and customer traction including OpenAI and AWS.
sZh: Cerebras Systems 的 IPO 招股书将其晶圆级引擎定位为全球最快的 AI 推理基础设施，称其推理速度比基于 GPU 的解决方案快 15 倍，营收从 2022 年的 2460 万美元增至 2025 年的 5.10 亿美元，并已获得 OpenAI 和 AWS 等客户。
absEn: Cerebras Systems' IPO prospectus presents the company as the builder of the world's fastest AI infrastructure, centered on its Wafer-Scale Engine, the first and only commercialized wafer-scale processor, which is 58 times larger than NVIDIA's B200 chip and delivers up to 15 times faster inference than leading GPU-based solutions. The core argument is that AI has entered an inference-centric era in which reasoning models perform substantial computation during inference, making speed a necessity rather than a luxury: faster inference improves user engagement, expands the range of addressable tasks, and creates switching costs as user expectations for interactivity rise. Cerebras supports this thesis with customer traction, including OpenAI's selection of its fast inference solution and a binding term sheet with AWS, alongside revenue growth from $24.6 million in 2022 to $510.0 million in 2025. The prospectus concludes that AI inference will grow more than twice as fast as AI training infrastructure through 2029, and that Cerebras is well-positioned to capture growth across both markets given its benchmarked inference leadership and large-scale training track record.
absZh: Cerebras Systems 的 IPO 招股书将该公司定位为全球最快 AI 基础设施的构建者，其核心是晶圆级引擎（Wafer-Scale Engine）——首个也是唯一实现商业化的晶圆级处理器，面积是英伟达 B200 芯片的 58 倍，推理速度最高可达领先 GPU 解决方案的 15 倍。其核心论点是：AI 已进入以推理为中心的时代，推理模型在推理过程中执行大量计算，因此速度不再是奢侈品而是必需品——更快的推理能提升用户参与度、拓展可处理任务的范围，并随着用户对交互性期望的提高而形成转换成本。Cerebras 以客户进展支撑这一论点，包括 OpenAI 选择其快速推理解决方案、与 AWS 签署具有约束力的条款清单，以及营收从 2022 年的 2460 万美元增长至 2025 年的 5.10 亿美元。招股书总结称，到 2029 年，AI 推理的增长速度将超过 AI 训练基础设施的两倍以上，而凭借经基准测试验证的推理领先地位和大规模训练记录，Cerebras 已做好充分准备，把握这两个市场的增长机遇。

contrib.en: Revenue grew from $24.6M in 2022 to $510.0M in 2025, up 76% year over year.
contrib.zh: 营收从 2022 年的 2460 万美元增至 2025 年的 5.10 亿美元，同比增长 76%。

contrib.en: WSE-3 is 58x larger than NVIDIA's B200 chip, with 2,625x more memory bandwidth.
contrib.zh: WSE-3 芯片面积是英伟达 B200 的 58 倍，内存带宽高出 2,625 倍。

contrib.en: Cerebras Inference delivers answers up to 15x faster than leading GPU-based solutions.
contrib.zh: Cerebras 推理服务比领先的 GPU 方案快至多 15 倍。

contrib.en: OpenAI selected Cerebras as its fast inference solution; AWS signed a binding term sheet.
contrib.zh: OpenAI 选择 Cerebras 作为其快速推理方案；AWS 签署了有约束力的条款清单。

contrib.en: Net income was $237.8M in 2025 versus a $481.6M net loss in 2024.
contrib.zh: 2025 年净利润 2.378 亿美元，而 2024 年净亏损 4.816 亿美元。

contrib.en: Top ten customers raised aggregate spend about 80% within 12 months of first purchase.
contrib.zh: 前十大客户在首次采购后 12 个月内将总支出提高约 80%。

limits.en: Revenue is concentrated in a few customers, including OpenAI, G42, MBZUAI, and AWS.
limits.zh: 营收集中于少数客户，包括 OpenAI、G42、MBZUAI 和 AWS。

limits.en: History of net losses; non-GAAP net loss was $75.7M in 2025 and $21.8M in 2024.
limits.zh: 公司历来净亏损；2025 年非 GAAP 净亏损 7570 万美元，2024 年为 2180 万美元。

limits.en: Material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting were identified.
limits.zh: 公司已识别出财务报告内部控制存在重大缺陷。

limits.en: Class B holders will control about 99.2% of voting power after the offering.
limits.zh: 发行后 B 类股股东将控制约 99.2%的投票权。

limits.en: Depends on third-party and sole-source suppliers with no capacity or volume commitments.
limits.zh: 依赖第三方及单一来源供应商，且无产能或采购量承诺。

paras.en: In 2015, we saw AI on the horizon and knew it would consume vast amounts of compute.
paras.zh: 2015 年，我们看到了 AI 的曙光，并深知它将消耗海量算力。

paras.en: AI was a new and unusual workload. And, for computer architects, new workloads create opportunities by forcing tectonic market shifts.
paras.zh: AI 是一种全新且不同寻常的工作负载。而对于计算机架构师而言，新的工作负载会迫使市场发生根本性转变，从而创造机遇。

paras.en: The founders made two fundamental bets.
paras.zh: 创始人做出了两个根本性判断。

paras.en: The first bet: that existing general-purpose processors would not be sufficient, and that what has always been true throughout the history of compute would also be true for AI – that transformative compute workloads require purpose-built silicon. This is what PCs did for x86, graphics did for GPUs, and mobile did for ARM.
paras.zh: 第一个判断：现有的通用处理器将无法满足需求，而算力发展史上始终成立的一条规律同样适用于 AI——具有变革性的算力工作负载需要专用芯片。这正是 PC 之于 x86、图形处理之于 GPU、移动设备之于 ARM 所发生的情形。

paras.en: The second bet: that modifying existing compute architectures would not realize AI’s potential. We would need to build a new computer architecture from first principles, optimized in every way for AI.
paras.zh: 第二个判断：对现有算力架构进行改造无法释放 AI 的潜力。我们需要从基本原理出发构建全新的计算机架构，并在各个方面针对 AI 进行优化。

paras.en: Both bets were contrarian. And both turned out to be right.
paras.zh: 这两个判断在当时都逆主流而行。而事实证明，两者都是正确的。

full.sec: Bigger is Better, Many Times Better

paras.en: At a computational level, graphics is a parallelism-bound problem and mobile is a power-bound problem. But AI is a communication-bound problem.
paras.zh: 在计算层面上，图形是一个受并行度约束的问题，而移动端是一个受功耗约束的问题。但 AI 是一个受通信约束的问题。

paras.en: The faster compute communicates with memory, and the faster compute communicates with other compute, the faster and smarter the AI, and the better the user experience.
paras.zh: 算力与内存通信的速度越快，算力与其他算力通信的速度越快，AI 就越快、越智能，用户体验就越好。

paras.en: The enemy of speed is communication latency. And since communication is thousand s of times faster on-chip, than across chips, the best way to reduce latency is to keep communication on-chip.
paras.zh: 速度的敌人是通信延迟。而由于片上通信比跨芯片通信快数千倍，降低延迟的最佳方式就是将通信保持在片上。

paras.en: Our answer: build the largest commercial chip in the history of the computer industry. We used the entire wafer for one chip: a technique called wafer-scale integration.
paras.zh: 我们的答案：打造计算机行业历史上最大的商用芯片。我们将整片晶圆用于一颗芯片：这项技术被称为晶圆级集成。

paras.en: Wafer-scale integration allowed us to bring together quantities of compute and memory never before assembled on a single commercial chip and deliver AI at previously unimaginable speeds. We could avoid the latency and the power-draw induced by the traditional approach of chopping up the AI problem and spreading it across lots of little chips.
paras.zh: 晶圆级集成使我们能够将前所未有的海量算力和内存汇聚到单颗商用芯片上，并以此前难以想象的速度交付 AI。我们可以避免传统做法——将 AI 问题切分并分散到众多小芯片上——所引发的延迟和功耗。

paras.en: It was a logical approach in principle, but it was also a daunting challenge in practice. Wafer-scale integration was one of the holy grails of computer architecture. Every previous effort to commercialize it had failed.
paras.zh: 从原理上讲，这是一种合乎逻辑的方法，但在实践中也是一项艰巨的挑战。晶圆级集成曾是计算机体系结构的圣杯之一。此前每一次将其商业化的尝试都以失败告终。

paras.en: We had to prove it was possible: to design it, fabricate it, yield it, power it, and run production workloads on it. This was a complex, multi-dimensional technical challenge: one that cut across chip design, system design, high performance software, and AI algorithms.
paras.zh: 我们必须证明它切实可行：完成设计、制造、良率提升、供电，并在其上运行生产工作负载。这是一项复杂的、多维度的技术挑战：它横跨芯片设计、系统设计、高性能软件和 AI 算法。

paras.en: When we set out to do it, nobody knew how to make it work.
paras.zh: 当我们着手去做时，没有人知道如何让它成功运转。

paras.en: Nobody knew how to yield a chip 58 times larger than the leading GPU. Nobody knew how to deliver power to a chip the size of a dinner plate without melting the motherboard. Nobody knew how to package such a big chip without cracking it. Nobody knew how to cool a chip of this size, with air or water, without the coolant getting warm before it reached the other side. Nobody knew, and we didn’t know.
paras.zh: 没有人知道如何产出一颗比领先 GPU 大 58 倍的芯片。没有人知道如何为一颗餐盘大小的芯片供电而不烧毁主板。没有人知道如何封装如此巨大的芯片而不使其开裂。没有人知道如何为这种尺寸的芯片散热——无论风冷还是水冷——而不让冷却液在到达另一侧之前就变热。没有人知道，我们也不知道。

paras.en: Many pointed out challenges they said were impossible to solve. But ironically, those weren’t the hardest challenges we had to solve. The hardest challenges were ones nobody had ever seen, because no one had ever progressed that far.
paras.zh: 许多人指出了他们声称无法解决的挑战。但讽刺的是，那些并不是我们必须解决的最困难的挑战。最困难的挑战是没有人曾见过的挑战，因为从未有人推进到那么远。

paras.en: Fundamental invention is profoundly difficult. We failed for a long time.
paras.zh: 根本性的发明极其艰难。我们失败了很长时间。

paras.en: But we believe in fearless engineering combined with relentless drive. It’s not just our culture. It is who we are. We attacked the unknown with a disciplined methodology: first principle analysis, experimentation, failure, failure analysis. Rinse and repeat.
paras.zh: 但我们相信无畏的工程精神与不懈的驱动力相结合。这不仅是我们的文化。这就是我们的本质。我们以严谨的方法论攻克未知：第一性原理分析、实验、失败、失败分析。如此循环往复。

paras.en: We believe that enduring moats are built by solving hard technical problems with novel solutions. Wafer-scale integration is one such moat that took a decade of invention and engineering to achieve.
paras.zh: 我们相信，持久的护城河是通过用新颖的解决方案解决艰难的技术问题而建立的。晶圆级集成就是这样一条护城河，它花费了十年的发明与工程才得以实现。

paras.en: We delivered our first systems in 2020 and the second generation in 2022. We had built something extraordinary, but the market wasn’t ready. A few visionary customers in supercompute and life sciences saw the potential, but to most of the world, the benefits were not immediately apparent.
paras.zh: 我们于 2020 年交付了首批系统，并于 2022 年交付了第二代系统。我们打造出了非凡的产品，但市场尚未做好准备。超算和生命科学领域的少数富有远见的客户看到了其潜力，但对世界上的大多数人而言，其优势并非显而易见。

paras.en: AI was nascent. It was raw and unproven. Training was time-consuming, a black art, and the domain of a select few. GPUs were not yet the bottleneck. And our solutions struggled to find a home.
paras.zh: AI 当时尚处萌芽阶段。它原始而未经检验。训练耗时漫长，是一门玄妙的技艺，且仅为少数人所掌握。GPU 当时尚未成为瓶颈。而我们的解决方案也难以找到用武之地。

paras.en: Change arrived with ChatGPT. Suddenly everyone was talking about AI, and entrepreneurs were extending the art of the possible. By early 2025, AI was smart enough to be valuable, and people were using AI everywhere. Inference usage exploded.
paras.zh: 变化随 ChatGPT 而来。突然间人人都在谈论 AI，创业者们不断拓展着可能性的边界。到 2025 年初，AI 已经足够智能、足够有价值，人们开始在各处使用 AI。推理用量呈爆发式增长。

paras.en: Suddenly, everyone remembered the lesson from Google search: speed produces more satisfied and more frequent users, while even tiny delays significantly reduce user satisfaction, search frequency, and search revenue.
paras.zh: 突然间，所有人都想起了 Google 搜索的教训：速度带来更满意、更频繁的用户，而即便是极微小的延迟也会显著降低用户满意度、搜索频率和搜索收入。

paras.en: The market had shifted. Everyone realized that fast AI is more useful than slow AI. By the end of 2025, it was clear: fast inference was powering the highest-value workloads. Fast inference was making engineers more productive because fast AI coding agents could write code, edit it, test it, and get a product to market more quickly. Fast AI made lawyers, analysts, bankers, doctors, and researchers more productive than their counterparts waiting on slow insights.
paras.zh: 市场已经转变。所有人都意识到，快速的 AI 比缓慢的 AI 更有用。到 2025 年底，这一点已十分明确：快速推理正在支撑最高价值的工作负载。快速推理让工程师的生产力更高，因为快速的 AI 编程智能体能够编写代码、编辑代码、测试代码，并更快地将产品推向市场。快速 AI 让律师、分析师、银行家、医生和研究人员的生产力高于那些等待缓慢洞察的同行。

paras.en: And so the flywheel started: as fast AI produced better answers in less time, users would do more with it, stay longer, and run higher-value workloads. Cerebras’s original vision to accelerate AI with custom silicon, systems, and software finally met a market that urgently needed—and demanded—the fast AI our innovations make possible.
paras.zh: 于是飞轮开始转动：随着快速 AI 在更短时间内给出更好的答案，用户会用它做更多的事、停留更久、运行更高价值的工作负载。Cerebras 以定制芯片、系统和软件加速 AI 的初心，终于遇上了一个迫切需要、并且要求快速 AI 的市场——而我们的创新让这种快速 AI 成为可能。

paras.en: **Our speed separates us from other AI infrastructure players.**
paras.zh: **我们的速度使我们区别于其他 AI 基础设施参与者。**

paras.en: For many workloads, Cerebras is up to 15 times faster than leading GPU-based solutions as benchmarked on leading open-source models. In some more exotic workloads, we have been more than 1,000 times faster. When customers experienced that speed for themselves, they knew they had to have it; we won new customers, and existing customers reordered, then reordered again.
paras.zh: 在许多工作负载上，以领先的开源模型为基准测试，Cerebras 比领先的基于 GPU 的解决方案快最多 15 倍。在一些更为特殊的工作负载上，我们的速度超过 1,000 倍。当客户亲身感受到这种速度时，他们知道自己必须拥有它；我们赢得了新客户，现有客户再次下单，然后又再次下单。

paras.en: Smarter models combined with fast inference makes AI more productive. And since tokens are how AI converts compute into intelligence, token consumption is growing exponentially. And because Cerebras generates tokens faster, we believe we are extraordinarily well-positioned to win in this market.
paras.zh: 更智能的模型结合快速推理，使 AI 更具生产力。而由于 token 是 AI 将算力转化为智能的方式，token 消耗量正呈指数级增长。又因为 Cerebras 生成 token 的速度更快，我们相信我们在这个市场中处于极其有利的制胜位置。

paras.en: In January 2026, we announced a multi-year deal with OpenAI valued at more than $20 billion dollars. OpenAI has agreed to deploy 750 megawatts of Cerebras’s high-speed AI compute, and OpenAI and Cerebras have agreed to co-design future models for future Cerebras hardware.
paras.zh: 2026 年 1 月，我们宣布与 OpenAI 达成一项价值超过$20 billion 的多年协议。OpenAI 已同意部署 750 兆瓦的 Cerebras 高速 AI 算力，且 OpenAI 与 Cerebras 已同意为未来的 Cerebras 硬件共同设计未来模型。

paras.en: In March 2026, we started a multi-year partnership with AWS to bring fast inference to an even bigger scale through global distribution. We’re aiming to give every startup, AI native, and enterprise company easy access to Cerebras’s blisteringly fast inference.
paras.zh: 2026 年 3 月，我们与 AWS 启动了多年合作伙伴关系，通过全球分销将快速推理扩展至更大规模。我们的目标是让每一家初创公司、AI 原生企业和企业公司都能轻松获得 Cerebras 极速的推理能力。

paras.en: We firmly believe that once you go fast, you can never go back. How much would we need to pay you to go back to slow internet?
paras.zh: 我们坚信，一旦体验过速度，就再也回不去了。要让你回到慢速互联网，我们需要付你多少钱？

paras.en: The explosion in AI usage profoundly changed the market. Cerebras was ready: meeting the changing needs of our customers and quickly adapting our business model. We made it easy for our customers to consume AI compute. We were among the first semi-conductor companies to have a cloud business. We deliver hardware on-premises to customers concerned about data security and sovereignty. And we reach other customers through the cloud – both the Cerebras cloud and soon the AWS cloud. This allows us to reach customers who want to rent compute by month, year, or to pay by the token, and provides Cerebras with an attractive mix of recurring revenue as well as lumpier hardware revenue.
paras.zh: AI 使用的爆发式增长深刻改变了市场。Cerebras 已做好准备：满足客户不断变化的需求，并迅速调整我们的商业模式。我们让客户能够轻松消费 AI 算力。我们是最早拥有云业务的半导体公司之一。我们向关注数据安全和主权的客户提供本地部署硬件。我们还通过云——包括 Cerebras 云以及即将推出的 AWS 云——触达其他客户。这使我们能够触达希望按月、按年租用算力或按 token 付费的客户，并为 Cerebras 提供有吸引力的经常性收入与波动较大的硬件收入组合。

paras.en: As we look forward, we will continue to engage in fearless engineering aimed at solving the hardest technical problems – the ones that create fundamental differentiation, customer value, and durable moats.
paras.zh: 展望未来，我们将继续投身于无畏的工程实践，致力于解决最艰难的技术问题——那些能够创造根本性差异化、客户价值和持久护城河的问题。

paras.en: We believe that shareholder value comes from doing the things customers want, but others cannot do. We will focus relentlessly on these items, make bold decisions, and weigh tradeoffs in favor of long-term value creation.
paras.zh: 我们相信，股东价值源于做客户想要、但他人做不到的事情。我们将不懈聚焦于这些事项，做出大胆决策，并在权衡取舍时优先考虑长期价值创造。

paras.en: We’re proud of our accomplishments, and we have inventions underway that build on and extend our advantages.
paras.zh: 我们为取得的成就感到自豪，并且我们已有在研发明，能够巩固并拓展我们的优势。

paras.en: The fundamental building blocks in computer architecture are calculation (cores), the storage of results (memory), and the movements of results to where they are needed (communication). Wafer-scale integration has provided a platform for more cores than any previous commercialized processor. It allows us to use memory in ways that are foreclosed to traditional sized processors. Our inventions are blurring the lines that have traditionally forced tradeoffs between memory capacity and speed. And the massive size of our processor serves as a foundation for pioneering communication techniques that are only available to wafer scale solutions.
paras.zh: 计算机体系结构的基本构件是计算（核心）、结果的存储（内存）以及结果向所需之处的移动（通信）。晶圆级集成提供了一个平台，其核心数量超过以往任何已商业化的处理器。它使我们能够以传统尺寸处理器无法企及的方式使用内存。我们的发明正在模糊传统上迫使内存容量与速度之间做出取舍的界限。而我们处理器的巨大尺寸，为只有晶圆级方案才能实现的开创性通信技术奠定了基础。

paras.en: Smarter models and faster inference are transforming entire sectors of the economy. The way we write software has changed forever. But we believe we have yet to fully contemplate the growing landscape for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and other latency-sensitive applications. These applications will continue to push fast inference demand, present novel challenges, and take the industry in new directions.
paras.zh: 更智能的模型和更快的推理正在改变整个经济领域。我们编写软件的方式已经永远改变。但我们认为，我们尚未充分思考自动驾驶汽车、机器人及其他对延迟敏感的应用日益增长的图景。这些应用将继续推动快速推理需求，带来新的挑战，并引领行业走向新的方向。

paras.en: **The AI market is moving extraordinarily quickly, and we are well-positioned to anticipate its twists and turns.**
paras.zh: **AI 市场正以极快的速度发展，我们处于有利位置，能够预判其曲折变化。**

paras.en: Our insights are now informed by a decade of pioneering invention, unique expertise in technologies that underpin fast AI, learning from our customers, and deploying some of the largest AI clusters in the world. Our partnerships provide not only visibility into the future, but also a chance to co-design hardware with those creating it.
paras.zh: 我们的洞察如今得益于十年的开创性发明、在支撑快速 AI 的技术方面的独特专长、向客户学习，以及部署世界上一些最大的 AI 集群。我们的合作伙伴关系不仅让我们洞见未来，还提供了与硬件创造者共同设计硬件的契机。

paras.en: We invite you to join us on this extraordinary journey through a technological revolution more profound than any that has come before.
paras.zh: 我们邀请您加入这场非凡旅程，共同经历一场比以往任何一次都更为深远的技术革命。

paras.en: Nothing excites us more than the future of AI.
paras.zh: 没有什么比 AI 的未来更令我们兴奋。

paras.en: We are grateful to our families for their patience, our team for their passion and hard work, our investors for their support and encouragement, and our customers and partners for their trust. To all those who have been with us through the first chapter in Cerebras’s life, we say thank you.
paras.zh: 我们感谢家人的耐心、团队的热情与辛勤付出、投资者的支持与鼓励，以及客户和合作伙伴的信任。对于所有在 Cerebras 生命第一章中与我们同行的人，我们致以感谢。

paras.en: And it is with great pride that we set off on the next chapter.
paras.zh: 我们无比自豪地开启下一章。
