paras.en: - changes in the financial projections we provide to the public or our failure to meet these projections;
paras.zh: - 我们向公众提供的财务预测发生变化，或我们未能达到这些预测；

paras.en: - failure of securities analysts to initiate or maintain coverage of us, changes in financial estimates by any securities analysts who follow our company, or our failure to meet the estimates or the expectations of investors or analysts;
paras.zh: - 证券分析师未能启动或维持对我们的覆盖、跟踪本公司的任何证券分析师对财务估计的调整，或我们未能达到投资者或分析师的估计或预期；

paras.en: - the economy as a whole and market conditions in our industry;
paras.zh: - 整体经济状况及我们所在行业的市场状况；

paras.en: - rumors and market speculation, and operating results and forecasts, involving us or other companies in our industry;
paras.zh: - 涉及我们或我们行业内其他公司的传闻和市场猜测，以及经营业绩和预测；

paras.en: - announcements by us or our competitors of significant innovations, acquisitions, strategic partnerships, joint ventures, or capital commitments;
paras.zh: - 我们或我们的竞争对手宣布重大创新、收购、战略合作、合资企业或资本承诺；

paras.en: - new laws or regulations or new interpretations of existing laws or regulations applicable to our business;
paras.zh: - 适用于我们业务的新法律或法规，或对现有法律或法规的新解释；

paras.en: - lawsuits threatened or filed against us;
paras.zh: - 针对我们提起或威胁提起的诉讼；

paras.en: - recruitment or departure of key personnel;
paras.zh: - 关键人员的招聘或离职；

paras.en: - changes in the U.S. regulatory environment impacting jurisdictions with which we can transact;
paras.zh: - 美国监管环境的变化，影响我们可与之开展交易的司法管辖区；

paras.en: - other events or factors, including those resulting from war, incidents of terrorism, or responses to these events;
paras.zh: - 其他事件或因素，包括战争、恐怖主义事件或对这些事件的应对所导致的事件或因素；

paras.en: - conversions of shares of Class B common stock or non-voting Class N common stock into shares of Class A common stock; and
paras.zh: - B 类普通股或无表决权 N 类普通股转换为 A 类普通股；以及

paras.en: - anticipated sales of our common stock, including upon lock-up releases and the expiration of lock-up agreements or market standoff provisions described elsewhere in this prospectus.
paras.zh: - 我们普通股的预期出售，包括本招股说明书其他部分所述锁定期解除以及锁定期协议或市场禁售条款到期时的出售。

paras.en: In addition, extreme price and volume fluctuations in the stock markets have affected and continue to affect many semiconductor, AI, and technology companies’ stock prices. Often, their stock prices have fluctuated in ways unrelated or disproportionate to the companies’ operating performance. The AI industry has also experienced rapid growth and seen high valuations that have caused stock price volatility related to speculation of the industry’s future growth and performance. In the past, stockholders have filed securities class action litigation following periods of market volatility. If we were to become involved in securities litigation, it could subject us to substantial costs, divert resources and the attention of management from our business and harm our business. Moreover, because of these fluctuations, comparing our results of operations on a period-to-period basis may not be meaningful. You should not rely on our past results as an indication of our future performance. This variability and unpredictability could also result in our failing to meet the expectations of industry or financial analysts or investors for any period. If our revenue or results of operations fall below the expectations of analysts or investors or below any forecasts we may provide to the market, or if the forecasts we provide to the market are below the expectations of analysts or investors, the price of our Class A common stock could decline substantially. Such a stock price decline could occur even when we have met any previously publicly stated revenue or earnings forecasts that we may provide.
paras.zh: 此外，股票市场的极端价格和成交量波动已经并继续影响许多半导体、AI 和科技公司的股价。这些公司的股价经常以与公司经营业绩无关或不成比例的方式波动。AI 行业也经历了快速增长并出现了高估值，导致股价因对行业未来增长和业绩的投机而波动。过去，股东曾在市场波动期后提起证券集体诉讼。如果我们卷入证券诉讼，可能使我们承担巨额成本，分散资源和管理层对业务的注意力，并损害我们的业务。此外，由于这些波动，逐期比较我们的经营业绩可能没有意义。您不应依赖我们的过往业绩作为我们未来业绩的指示。这种可变性和不可预测性还可能导致我们在任何期间未能达到行业或金融分析师或投资者的预期。如果我们的收入或经营业绩低于分析师或投资者的预期，或低于我们可能向市场提供的任何预测，或者如果我们向市场提供的预测低于分析师或投资者的预期，我们的 A 类普通股价格可能大幅下跌。即使我们已达到此前公开声明的、我们可能提供的任何收入或盈利预测，这种股价下跌仍可能发生。

paras.en: **No public market for our common stock currently exists and an active liquid market may not develop or be sustained following this offering.**
paras.zh: **我们的普通股目前不存在公开市场，且本次发行后可能不会形成或维持活跃的流动性市场。**

paras.en: No public market for our common stock currently exists. An active public trading market for our Class A common stock may not develop following the closing of this offering or, if developed, it may not be sustained. The lack of an active market may impair your ability to sell your shares at the time you wish to sell them or at a price that you consider reasonable. The lack of an active market may also reduce the fair value of your shares. An inactive market may also impair our ability to raise capital to continue to fund operations by selling securities and may impair our ability to acquire other companies or technologies by using our securities as consideration.
paras.zh: 我们的普通股目前不存在公开市场。本次发行结束后，我们的 A 类普通股可能不会形成活跃的公开交易市场，或者即使形成，也可能无法维持。缺乏活跃市场可能损害您在希望出售股份时或以您认为合理的价格出售股份的能力。缺乏活跃市场还可能降低您股份的公允价值。不活跃的市场还可能损害我们通过出售证券筹集资金以持续为运营提供资金的能力，并可能损害我们通过使用证券作为对价收购其他公司或技术的能力。

paras.en: **Future sales of our Class A common stock in the public market could cause the price of our common stock to decline.**
paras.zh: **我们的 A 类普通股未来在公开市场的出售可能导致我们普通股的价格下跌。**

paras.en: Sales of a substantial number of shares of our Class A common stock in the public market, particularly sales by our directors, executive officers, and principal stockholders, or the perception that these sales might occur, could cause the price of our Class A common stock to decline and could impair our ability to raise capital through the sale of additional equity securities.
paras.zh: 在公开市场大量出售我们的 A 类普通股，尤其是由我们的董事、高级管理人员和主要股东进行的出售，或市场认为此类出售可能发生，可能导致我们的 A 类普通股价格下跌，并可能损害我们通过出售额外股权证券筹集资金的能力。

paras.en: We, all of our directors and executive officers, and the holders of substantially all of our shares of Class A common stock outstanding and securities exercisable for or convertible into shares of our Class A common stock, have entered into lock-up agreements with the underwriters and/or agreements with market standoff provisions that restrict our and their ability to sell or transfer shares of our capital stock and securities convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for shares of our capital stock, for a period ending on the earlier of (i) 6:00 a.m. Eastern Time on the second trading day following our release of earnings for the quarter ending September 30, 2026 or (ii) 180 days after the date of this prospectus (the “Lock-up Period”), subject to certain customary exceptions and provisions that provide for the early release of certain of our securities during the Lock-up Period. In connection with such early-release provisions, we estimate an aggregate of up to approximately 171.1 million shares will be released from lock-up agreements or market standoff provisions during the Lock-up Period, including up to approximately 15.0 million shares held by our directors and officers subject to reporting under Section 16 of the Exchange Act. Furthermore, pursuant to certain exceptions to the lock-up agreements and market standoff provisions, certain shares of our Class A common stock will be eligible for sale in the open market during the Lock-up Period in sell-to-cover transactions in order to satisfy tax withholding obligations in connection with the settlement of RSUs. Pursuant to such exceptions, we estimate up to an aggregate of (i) 0.2 million shares and (ii) 0.4 million shares may be sold in the open market on or around June 24, 2026 and August 18, 2026, respectively (representing quarterly vesting of service-based RSUs), in connection with such tax withholding obligations (based on an assumed 46.9% tax withholding rate). In addition, certain exceptions to the lock-up agreements and market standoff provisions permit holders of stock options to sell shares of our Class A common stock on the open market to cover the tax obligations or payments due in connection with the exercise of such options. As of April 30, 2026, there were an aggregate of approximately 21.5 million vested stock options outstanding. Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, Citigroup Global Markets Inc., and Barclays Capital Inc., on behalf of the underwriters, may release any of the securities subject to these lock-up agreements and market standoff provisions at any time, subject to the applicable notice requirements. See the sections titled “Shares Eligible for Future Sale” and “Underwriters” for a discussion of exceptions and the early-release provisions that allow for sales during the Lock-up Period. Sales of a substantial number of shares during the Lock-up Period and upon the expiration of the Lock-up Period or the perception that such sales may occur could cause the price of our Class A common stock to fall or make it more difficult for an investor to sell our Class A common stock at a time and price that an investor deems appropriate. Shares held by directors, executive officers, and other affiliates will be subject to volume limitations under Rule 144 under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”).
paras.zh: 我们、我们全体董事和高级管理人员，以及我们几乎全部已发行在外 A 类普通股和可行使或可转换为 A 类普通股的证券的持有人，已与承销商签订锁定期协议和/或签订含有市场禁售条款的协议，限制我们及上述持有人出售或转让我们的股本股份以及可转换为、可行使或可交换为股本股份的证券，限制期截至以下两者中较早者：(i) 我们发布截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日止季度业绩后的第二个交易日美国东部时间上午 6:00，或(ii) 本招股说明书日期后 180 天（“锁定期”），但须遵守若干惯常例外情形及允许在锁定期内提前解禁我们部分证券的规定。就上述提前解禁规定而言，我们估计在锁定期内合计最多约 171.1 百万股将自锁定期协议或市场禁售条款中解禁，其中包括最多约 15.0 百万股由受《交易法》第 16 条申报要求约束的董事和高级管理人员持有的股份。此外，根据锁定期协议和市场禁售条款的若干例外情形，我们部分 A 类普通股将有资格在锁定期内通过卖出补税交易在公开市场出售，以满足与 RSU 结算相关的代扣税义务。根据上述例外情形，我们估计合计最多(i) 0.2 百万股和(ii) 0.4 百万股可能分别于 2026 年 6 月 24 日和 2026 年 8 月 18 日前后在公开市场出售（对应基于服务的 RSU 的季度归属），用于履行上述代扣税义务（基于假设的 46.9%代扣税率）。此外，锁定期协议和市场禁售条款的若干例外情形允许股票期权持有人为支付与行使该等期权相关的税务义务或应付款项而在公开市场出售我们的 A 类普通股。截至 2026 年 4 月 30 日，合计约有 21.5 百万份已归属且尚未行使的股票期权。Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC、Citigroup Global Markets Inc.和 Barclays Capital Inc.代表承销商，可在遵守适用通知要求的前提下随时解禁受该等锁定期协议和市场禁售条款约束的任何证券。有关例外情形及允许在锁定期内出售的提前解禁规定的讨论，请参见“未来可出售股份”和“承销商”章节。在锁定期内及锁定期届满时出售大量股份，或市场认为可能发生此类出售，可能导致我们的 A 类普通股价格下跌，或使投资者更难在投资者认为适当的时间和价格出售我们的 A 类普通股。董事、高级管理人员和其他关联方持有的股份将受经修订的 1933 年《证券法》（“《证券法》”）第 144 条规定的成交量限制约束。

paras.en: In addition, as of December 31, 2025, after giving effect to the Common Stock Reclassification and the RSU Net Settlement, we had stock options outstanding that, if fully exercised, would result in the issuance of 28,361,707 shares of our Class B common stock and 10,403,567 shares of our Class B common stock issuable upon vesting of outstanding RSUs. We intend to file one or more registration statements on Form S-8 under the Securities Act to register the shares of our common stock subject to outstanding stock options and RSUs, as of the date of this prospectus and shares that will be issuable pursuant to future awards granted under our equity incentive plans. Once we register these shares, they can be freely sold in the public market upon issuance, subject to applicable vesting requirements, compliance by affiliates with Rule 144, and other restrictions provided under the terms of the applicable plan and/or the award agreements entered into with participants.
paras.zh: 此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，在使普通股重新分类和 RSU 净额结算生效后，我们尚未行使的股票期权若全部行使，将导致发行 28,361,707 股我们的 B 类普通股，以及 10,403,567 股我们的 B 类普通股可在尚未归属的 RSU 归属时发行。我们拟根据《证券法》提交一份或多份 S-8 表格注册声明，以注册截至本招股说明书日期受尚未行使的股票期权和 RSU 约束的普通股股份，以及根据我们股权激励计划未来授予的奖励将可发行的股份。一旦我们注册这些股份，它们可在发行后在公开市场自由出售，但须遵守适用的归属要求、关联方遵守第 144 条规则以及适用计划和/或与参与者签订的奖励协议条款规定的其他限制。

paras.en: Following this offering, the holders of up to an aggregate of approximately 147.7 million shares of our common stock (excluding shares of our Class N common stock issued or issuable upon the exercise of the OpenAI Warrant) will have rights, subject to some conditions, to require us to file registration statements for the public resale of shares of the Class A common stock issuable upon conversion of such shares or to include such shares in registration statements that we may file for us or other stockholders. Any registration statement we file to register additional shares, whether as a result of registration rights or otherwise, could cause the price of our Class A common stock to decline or be volatile.
paras.zh: 本次发行后，合计最多约 147.7 百万股我们普通股的持有人（不包括已发行或可因行使 OpenAI 认股权证而发行的 N 类普通股股份）将享有在某些条件约束下要求我们提交注册声明以公开转售该等股份转换后可发行的 A 类普通股股份的权利，或要求将该等股份纳入我们可能为我们或其他股东提交的注册声明中的权利。我们为注册额外股份而提交的任何注册声明，无论是因注册权还是其他原因，均可能导致我们 A 类普通股的价格下跌或波动。

paras.en: **If you purchase shares of our Class A common stock in this offering, you will incur immediate and substantial dilution.**
paras.zh: **如果您在本次发行中购买我们的 A 类普通股股份，您将立即遭受重大稀释。**

paras.en: The initial public offering price is substantially higher than the pro forma net tangible book value per share of our Class A common stock immediately following this offering based on the total value of our tangible assets less our total liabilities. Therefore, if you purchase our Class A common stock in this offering at the initial public offering price of $185.00 per share, you will experience immediate dilution of $155.49 per share, the difference between the price per share you pay for our Class A common stock and our pro forma net tangible book value per share as of December 31, 2025, after giving effect to the issuance by us of shares of our Class A common stock in this offering, the Preferred Stock Conversion, the Common Stock Reclassification, and the RSU Net Settlement. In addition, you may also experience additional dilution if stock options, RSUs, PRSUs, warrants (including the OpenAI Warrant), stock appreciation rights (“SARs”), or other rights to purchase our common stock that are outstanding or that we may issue in the future are exercised, vest, or are converted or we issue additional shares of our common stock at prices lower than our net tangible book value at such time.
paras.zh: 首次公开发行价格大幅高于本次发行后立即按我们的有形资产总值减总负债计算的我们 A 类普通股每股备考净有形账面价值。因此，如果您在本次发行中以每股 $185.00 的首次公开发行价格购买我们的 A 类普通股，您将立即遭受每股 $155.49 的稀释，即您为我们的 A 类普通股支付的每股价格与截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日我们每股备考净有形账面价值之间的差额，该差额已使我们在本次发行中发行 A 类普通股股份、优先股转换、普通股重新分类和 RSU 净额结算生效。此外，如果尚未行使或我们未来可能发行的股票期权、RSU、PRSU、认股权证（包括 OpenAI 认股权证）、股票增值权（“SARs”）或其他购买我们普通股的权利被行使、归属或转换，或者我们以低于当时净有形账面价值的价格发行额外普通股股份，您还可能遭受额外稀释。

paras.en: **We have broad discretion in the use of the net proceeds from this offering and may not use them effectively.**
paras.zh: **我们在本次发行净收益的使用方面拥有广泛的自主权，且可能无法有效使用该等净收益。**

paras.en: We will have broad discretion in the application of the net proceeds to us from this offering, including for any of the purposes described in the section titled “Use of Proceeds,” and you will not have the opportunity as part of your investment decision to assess whether the net proceeds are being used appropriately. Because of the number and variability of factors that will determine our use of the net proceeds from this offering, our ultimate use may vary substantially from our currently intended use. Investors will need to rely on the judgment of our management with respect to the use of proceeds. Pending use, we may invest the net proceeds from this offering in short-term, investment-grade, interest-bearing securities, such as money market funds, corporate notes and bonds, certificates of deposit, commercial paper, and guaranteed obligations of the U.S. government that may not generate a high yield for our stockholders. If we do not use the net proceeds that we receive in this offering effectively, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects could be harmed, and the price of our Class A common stock could decline.
paras.zh: 我们将在本次发行所得净收益的用途上拥有广泛的自主决定权，包括用于标题为“所得收益用途”一节中所述的任何目的，而您作为投资决策的一部分，将没有机会评估净收益是否被恰当使用。由于决定我们使用本次发行净收益的因素数量众多且存在不确定性，我们的最终用途可能与目前预期的用途存在重大差异。投资者将需要依赖我们管理层对所得收益用途的判断。在收益使用之前，我们可能将本次发行所得净收益投资于短期、投资级、计息证券，例如货币市场基金、公司票据和债券、存单、商业票据以及美国政府的担保债务，这些投资可能不会为我们的股东带来高收益。如果我们未能有效使用本次发行所收到的净收益，我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和前景可能受到损害，我们的 A 类普通股价格可能下跌。

paras.en: **We will incur increased costs as a result of operating as a public company, and our management will be required to devote substantial time to support compliance with our public company responsibilities and corporate governance practices.**
paras.zh: **由于作为上市公司运营，我们将产生更高的成本，我们的管理层将被要求投入大量时间以支持遵守我们作为上市公司的责任和公司治理实践。**

paras.en: As a public company, we will incur significant finance, legal, accounting, and other expenses, including director and officer liability insurance, that we did not incur as a private company, and which we expect to further increase after we are no longer an “emerging growth company.” The Sarbanes-Oxley Act, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, stock exchange listing requirements, and other applicable securities rules and regulations impose various requirements on public companies in the United States. Our management and other personnel are expected to devote a substantial amount of time to support compliance with these requirements. Moreover, these rules and regulations will increase our legal and financial compliance costs, including hiring additional personnel, and will make some activities more time-consuming and costly. We cannot predict or estimate the amount of additional costs we will incur as a public company or the specific timing of such costs.
paras.zh: 作为上市公司，我们将产生重大的财务、法律、会计及其他费用，包括董事和高级职员责任保险，这些费用在我们作为私营公司时并未产生，并且我们预计在我们不再属于“新兴成长型公司”后这些费用将进一步增加。《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》、《多德-弗兰克华尔街改革和消费者保护法案》、证券交易所上市要求以及其他适用的证券规则和法规对美国上市公司施加了各种要求。我们的管理层和其他人员预计将投入大量时间以支持遵守这些要求。此外，这些规则和法规将增加我们的法律和财务合规成本，包括聘用额外人员，并将使某些活动更加耗时和昂贵。我们无法预测或估计作为上市公司将产生的额外成本金额或此类成本的具体时间。

paras.en: **We currently have no plans to pay dividends on our common stock.**
paras.zh: **我们目前没有计划就我们的普通股支付股息。**

paras.en: We have never declared or paid any cash dividends on shares of our capital stock. We currently intend to retain all available funds and any future earnings for use in the operation of our business and do not anticipate paying any dividends in the foreseeable future. Any determination to pay dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our board of directors and will depend on many factors, including our financial condition, results of operations, earnings, capital requirements, business expansion opportunities, level of indebtedness, statutory and contractual restrictions applying to the payment of dividends, and other considerations that our board of directors deem relevant. In addition, the Revolving Credit Agreement contains restrictions on our ability to pay cash dividends on our Class A common stock. Our ability to pay dividends may be further restricted by agreements we may enter into in the future. Accordingly, you may need to rely on sales of our Class A common stock after price appreciation, which may never occur, as the only way to realize any future gains on your investment.
paras.zh: 我们从未就我们的股本股份宣布或派发任何现金股息。我们目前拟将所有可用资金及任何未来收益留存用于经营我们的业务，且预计在可预见的未来不会派发任何股息。未来是否派发股息的任何决定将由我们的董事会酌情作出，并将取决于诸多因素，包括我们的财务状况、经营业绩、盈利、资本需求、业务扩张机会、负债水平、适用于股息派发的法定及合同限制，以及我们董事会认为相关的其他考量因素。此外，循环信贷协议对我们就 A 类普通股派发现金股息的能力作出了限制。我们派发股息的能力可能进一步受到我们未来可能签订的协议的限制。因此，您可能只能依赖在股价上涨后出售我们的 A 类普通股来实现投资的任何未来收益，而股价上涨可能永远不会发生。

paras.en: **If securities or industry analysts do not publish research or publish inaccurate or unfavorable research about our business, our stock price and trading volume could decline.**
paras.zh: **如果证券或行业分析师不发布研究报告，或发布关于我们业务的不准确或不利的研究报告，我们的股价和交易量可能会下降。**

paras.en: The trading market for our Class A common stock will be influenced by the research and reports that industry or financial analysts publish about us or our business. We do not control these analysts or the content and opinions included in their reports. As a new public company, we may be slow to attract research coverage, and the analysts who publish information about our Class A common stock will have had relatively little experience with our company, which could affect their ability to accurately forecast our results and make it more likely that we fail to meet their estimates. In the event we obtain industry or financial analyst coverage, if any of the analysts who cover us issues an inaccurate or unfavorable opinion regarding our stock price, our stock price may decline. In addition, the stock prices of many companies in the technology industry have declined significantly after those companies have failed to meet, or exceed, the financial guidance publicly announced by the companies or the expectations of analysts. If our results of operations fail to meet, or exceed, our announced guidance or the expectations of analysts or public investors, analysts could downgrade our Class A common stock or publish unfavorable research about us, and the price of our Class A common stock would likely decline as a result of such failure to meet our guidance or analyst expectations. If one or more of these analysts cease coverage of our Class A common stock or fail to publish reports on us regularly, our visibility in the financial markets could decrease, which in turn could cause our stock price or trading volume to decline.
paras.zh: 我们 A 类普通股的交易市场将受到行业或财务分析师发布的关于我们或我们业务的研究和报告的影响。我们无法控制这些分析师或他们报告中包含的内容和观点。作为一家新上市公司，我们吸引研究覆盖的速度可能较慢，而发布关于我们 A 类普通股信息的分析师对公司的了解相对较少，这可能影响他们准确预测我们业绩的能力，并使我们更有可能无法达到他们的预期。如果我们获得行业或财务分析师的覆盖，而任何覆盖我们的分析师就我们的股价发布不准确或不利的意见，我们的股价可能会下降。此外，技术行业许多公司的股价在未能达到或超过这些公司公开宣布的财务指引或分析师预期后大幅下跌。如果我们的经营业绩未能达到或超过我们宣布的指引或分析师或公众投资者的预期，分析师可能会下调我们 A 类普通股的评级或发布关于我们的不利研究报告，而我们的 A 类普通股价格可能因未能达到我们的指引或分析师预期而下降。如果一名或多名此类分析师停止覆盖我们的 A 类普通股或未能定期发布关于我们的报告，我们在金融市场中的可见度可能会降低，进而可能导致我们的股价或交易量下降。

paras.en: **For as long as we are an emerging growth company, we will not be required to comply with certain reporting requirements, including those relating to accounting standards and disclosure about our executive compensation, that apply to other public companies.**
paras.zh: **只要我们仍是一家新兴成长型公司，我们就不需要遵守适用于其他上市公司的某些报告要求，包括与会计准则及高管薪酬披露相关的要求。**

paras.en: We are an “emerging growth company,” as defined in the JOBS Act, and we may take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements that are applicable to other public companies that are not “emerging growth companies,” including the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404, reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in our periodic reports and proxy statements, and exemptions from the requirements of holding a nonbinding advisory vote on executive compensation and stockholder approval of any golden parachute payments not previously approved. Pursuant to Section 107 of the JOBS Act, as an emerging growth company, we have elected to use the extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. As a result, our consolidated financial statements may not be comparable to the financial statements of issuers who are required to comply with the effective dates for new or revised accounting standards that are applicable to public companies, which may make our Class A common stock less attractive to investors. In addition, if we cease to be an emerging growth company, we will no longer be able to use the extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards.
paras.zh: 我们是一家《JOBS 法案》所定义的“新兴成长型公司”，我们可能利用适用于其他非“新兴成长型公司”上市公司的多项报告要求豁免，包括第 404 条的审计师鉴证要求、在定期报告和委托书中关于高管薪酬的披露义务减免，以及豁免就高管薪酬举行不具约束力的咨询性投票和就任何未经事先批准的黄金降落伞付款寻求股东批准的要求。根据《JOBS 法案》第 107 条，作为新兴成长型公司，我们已选择采用延长的过渡期来遵守新的或修订的会计准则，直至这些准则原本适用于私营公司之时。因此，我们的合并财务报表可能无法与须遵守适用于上市公司的新的或修订会计准则生效日期的发行人的财务报表进行比较，这可能使我们的 A 类普通股对投资者吸引力下降。此外，如果我们不再是新兴成长型公司，我们将不再能够使用延长的过渡期来遵守新的或修订的会计准则。

paras.en: We will remain an emerging growth company until the first to occur of: (1) the last day of the year following the fifth anniversary of this offering; (2) the last day of the first year in which our annual gross revenue is $1.235 billion or more; (3) the date on which we have, during the previous rolling three-year period, issued more than $1.0 billion in non-convertible debt securities; and (4) the date we qualify as a “large accelerated filer,” with at least $700 million of equity securities held by non-affiliates.
paras.zh: 我们将一直作为新兴成长型公司，直至以下最早发生之日：(1) 本次发行五周年之后的当年最后一天；(2) 我们的年度总收入达到 $1.235 billion 或以上的首个年度的最后一天；(3) 我们在此前滚动三年期间发行超过 $1.0 billion 不可转换债务证券之日；以及 (4) 我们符合“大型加速申报人”资格、且非关联方持有的股权证券至少达到 $700 million 之日。

paras.en: We cannot predict if investors will find our Class A common stock less attractive if we choose to rely on these exemptions. For example, if we do not adopt a new or revised accounting standard, our future results of operations may not be as comparable to the results of operations of certain other companies in our industry that adopted such standards. If some investors find our Class A common stock less attractive as a result, there may be a less active trading market for our Class A common stock, and our stock price may be more volatile.
paras.zh: 我们无法预测，如果我们选择依赖这些豁免，投资者是否会认为我们的 A 类普通股吸引力下降。例如，如果我们不采用新的或修订的会计准则，我们未来的经营业绩可能无法与同行业中采用该等准则的某些其他公司的经营业绩进行比较。如果部分投资者因此认为我们的 A 类普通股吸引力下降，我们的 A 类普通股交易市场可能不够活跃，我们的股价可能更加波动。

paras.en: **Anti-takeover provisions contained in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws, as well as provisions of Delaware law, could impair a takeover attempt.**
paras.zh: **我们经修订和重述的公司章程以及经修订和重述的公司细则中所载的反收购条款，以及特拉华州法律的规定，可能妨碍收购尝试。**

paras.en: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, contain, and Delaware law contains, provisions which could have the effect of rendering more difficult, delaying, or preventing an acquisition deemed undesirable by our board of directors. These provisions will provide for the following:
paras.zh: 我们经修订和重述的公司章程以及经修订和重述的公司细则将于本次发行完成前立即生效，其中包含的条款以及特拉华州法律的规定，可能产生使我们的董事会认为不可取的收购变得更加困难、延迟或阻止的效果。这些条款将规定以下内容：

paras.en: - our multi-class structure of our capital stock, which provides holders of our Class B common stock with the ability to significantly influence the outcome of matters requiring stockholder approval, even if they own significantly less than a majority of the shares of our outstanding capital stock;
paras.zh: - 我们资本股的多类别结构，使我们的 B 类普通股持有人能够对需要股东批准的事项的结果产生重大影响，即使他们拥有的股份远少于我们已发行资本股的多数；

paras.en: - a classified board of directors with staggered three-year terms, which may delay the ability of stockholders to change the membership of a majority of our board of directors;
paras.zh: - 采用交错三年任期的分类董事会，这可能延迟股东更换我们董事会多数成员的能力；

paras.en: - no cumulative voting in the election of directors, which limits the ability of minority stockholders to elect director candidates;
paras.zh: - 董事选举中不采用累积投票制，这限制了少数股东选举董事候选人的能力；

paras.en: - the exclusive right of our board of directors to establish the size of the board of directors and to appoint a director to fill a vacancy, however occurring, including by expanding the board of directors;
paras.zh: - 我们董事会的专属权利，即确定董事会规模并任命董事填补任何原因产生的空缺，包括通过扩大董事会；

paras.en: - the ability of our board of directors to authorize the issuance of shares of preferred stock and to determine the price and other terms of those shares, including voting or other rights or preferences, without stockholder approval, which could be used to significantly dilute the ownership of a hostile acquiror;
paras.zh: - 我们董事会授权发行优先股股份并确定该等股份的价格和其他条款（包括投票权或其他权利或优先权）的能力，无需股东批准，这可能被用于大幅稀释敌意收购方的所有权；

paras.en: - the ability of our board of directors to alter our amended and restated bylaws without obtaining stockholder approval;
paras.zh: - 我们董事会无需获得股东批准即可修改我们经修订和重述的章程的能力；

paras.en: - supermajority voting requirement to amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws;
paras.zh: - 修改我们经修订和重述的公司注册证书和经修订和重述的章程中某些条款的绝对多数投票要求；

paras.en: - a prohibition on stockholder action by written consent, which forces stockholder action to be taken at an annual or special meeting of our stockholders;
paras.zh: - 禁止股东通过书面同意采取行动，这迫使股东行动须在我们的股东年度会议或特别会议上采取；

paras.en: - the requirement that a special meeting of stockholders may be called only by our Chief Executive Officer or a majority of our board of directors then in office, which may delay the ability of our stockholders to force consideration of a proposal or to take action, including the removal of directors;
paras.zh: - 股东特别会议只能由我们的首席执行官或当时在任的董事会多数成员召集的要求，这可能延迟我们股东迫使审议提案或采取行动（包括罢免董事）的能力；

paras.en: - advance notice procedures that stockholders must comply with in order to nominate candidates to our board of directors or to propose matters to be acted upon at a stockholders’ meeting, which may discourage or deter a potential acquiror from conducting a solicitation of proxies to elect the acquiror’s own slate of directors or otherwise attempting to obtain control of us; and
paras.zh: - 股东为向我们的董事会提名候选人或在股东会议上提出待采取行动的事项而必须遵守的提前通知程序，这可能阻碍或阻止潜在收购方进行代理权征集以选举收购方自己的董事名单或以其他方式试图获得对我们的控制；以及

paras.en: - the limitation of liability of, and provision of indemnification to, our directors and officers.
paras.zh: - 对我们董事和高级管理人员的责任限制和赔偿条款。

paras.en: These provisions, alone or together, could delay or prevent hostile takeovers and changes in control or changes in our management.
paras.zh: 这些条款单独或共同可能延迟或阻止敌意收购和控制权变更或我们管理层的变更。

paras.en: As a Delaware corporation, we are also subject to provisions of Delaware law, including Section 203 of the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware (the “Delaware General Corporation Law”), which prevents some stockholders holding more than 15% of our outstanding common stock from engaging in certain business combinations without approval of the holders of substantially all of our outstanding common stock. For a description of our capital stock, see the section titled “Description of Capital Stock.”
paras.zh: 作为一家特拉华州公司，我们还受特拉华州法律条款的约束，包括《特拉华州普通公司法》（“《特拉华州普通公司法》”）第 203 条，该条禁止某些持有我们已发行普通股超过 15% 的股东在未经我们绝大多数已发行普通股持有人批准的情况下进行某些业务合并。有关我们股本的描述，请参见标题为“股本描述”的章节。

paras.en: Any provision of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, amended and restated bylaws, or Delaware law that has the effect of delaying or deterring a change in control could limit the opportunity for our stockholders to receive a premium for their shares of our Class A common stock, and could also affect the price that some investors are willing to pay for our Class A common stock.
paras.zh: 我们的经修订和重述的公司章程、经修订和重述的章程细则或特拉华州法律的任何条款，如果具有延迟或阻止控制权变更的效果，可能会限制我们的股东就其持有的 A 类普通股获得溢价的机会，也可能影响某些投资者愿意为我们的 A 类普通股支付的价格。

paras.en: **Claims for indemnification by our directors and officers may reduce our available funds to satisfy successful third-party claims against us and may reduce the amount of money available to us.**
paras.zh: **我们的董事和高级管理人员提出的赔偿请求可能会减少我们可用于应对针对我们的成功第三方索赔的可用资金，并可能减少我们可用的资金金额。**

paras.en: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, provide that we will indemnify our directors and officers, in each case to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law.
paras.zh: 我们的经修订和重述的公司章程和经修订和重述的章程细则将在本次发行完成前立即生效，其中规定我们将按照特拉华州法律允许的最大限度对我们的董事和高级管理人员进行赔偿。

paras.en: In addition, as permitted by Section 145 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, our amended and restated bylaws to be effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, and our indemnification agreements that we have entered or intend to enter into with our directors and officers provide that:
paras.zh: 此外，根据《特拉华州普通公司法》第 145 条的允许，我们将在本次发行完成前立即生效的经修订和重述的章程细则，以及我们已与或拟与我们的董事和高级管理人员签订的赔偿协议规定：

paras.en: - we will indemnify our directors and officers for serving us in those capacities or for serving other business enterprises at our request to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law. Delaware law provides that a corporation may indemnify such person if such person acted in good faith and in a manner such person reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the registrant and, with respect to any criminal proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe such person’s conduct was unlawful;
paras.zh: - 我们将按照特拉华州法律允许的最大限度，对我们的董事和高级管理人员以该等身份为我们服务或应我们请求为其他企业提供服务进行赔偿。特拉华州法律规定，如果该等人员本着善意行事，并以该人员合理认为符合或至少不违背注册人最佳利益的方式行事，且在任何刑事诉讼中，没有合理理由相信该人员的行为违法，则公司可以对该等人员进行赔偿；

paras.en: - we may, in our discretion, indemnify employees and agents in those circumstances where indemnification is permitted by applicable law;
paras.zh: - 在适用法律允许赔偿的情况下，我们可以自行决定对员工和代理人进行赔偿；

paras.en: - we are required to advance expenses, as incurred, to our directors and officers in connection with defending a proceeding, except that such directors or officers will undertake to repay such advances if it is ultimately determined that such person is not entitled to indemnification;
paras.zh: - 我们需要在董事和高级管理人员就抗辩程序发生费用时预支该等费用，但前提是该等董事或高级管理人员承诺，如果最终确定该人员无权获得赔偿，则将偿还该等预支款项；

paras.en: - the rights conferred in our amended and restated bylaws are not exclusive, and we are authorized to enter into indemnification agreements with our directors, officers, employees, and agents and to obtain insurance to indemnify such persons; and
paras.zh: - 我们的经修订和重述的章程细则所赋予的权利并非排他性的，我们有权与我们的董事、高级管理人员、员工和代理人签订赔偿协议，并购买保险以对该等人员进行赔偿；以及

paras.en: - we may not retroactively amend our amended and restated bylaw provisions to reduce our indemnification obligations to directors, officers, employees, and agents.
paras.zh: - 我们不得追溯修订我们的经修订和重述的章程细则条款，以减少我们对董事、高级管理人员、员工和代理人的赔偿义务。

paras.en: While we maintain a directors’ and officers’ insurance policy, such insurance may not be adequate to cover all liabilities that we may incur, which may reduce our available funds to satisfy third-party claims and may harm our business and financial position.

paras.en: **Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide for an exclusive forum in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware for certain disputes between us and our stockholders, and that the federal district courts of the United States will be the exclusive forum for the resolution of any complaint asserting a cause of action under the Securities Act.**
paras.zh: **我们经修订和重述的公司章程以及经修订和重述的章程细则将规定，对于我们与股东之间的某些争议，特拉华州衡平法院为专属管辖法院，并规定美国联邦地区法院为就《证券法》项下诉讼请求提出任何投诉的专属管辖法院。**

paras.en: Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, will provide, that: (i) unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if such court does not have subject matter jurisdiction thereof, the federal district court of the State of Delaware) will, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for: (A) any derivative action or proceeding brought on behalf of the company, (B) any action asserting a claim for or based on a breach of a fiduciary duty owed by any of our current or former directors, officers, other employees, agents, or stockholders to the company or our stockholders, including without limitation a claim alleging the aiding and abetting of such a breach of fiduciary duty, (C) any action asserting a claim against the company or any of our current or former directors, officers, employees, agents, or stockholders arising pursuant to any provision of the Delaware General Corporation Law or our certificate of incorporation or bylaws or as to which the Delaware General Corporation Law confers jurisdiction on the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware, or (D) any action asserting a claim related to or involving the company that is governed by the internal affairs doctrine; (ii) unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United States will, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for the resolution of any complaint asserting a cause of action arising under the Securities Act, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder; (iii) any person or entity purchasing or otherwise acquiring or holding any interest in shares of capital stock of the company will be deemed to have notice of and consented to these provisions; and (iv) failure to enforce the foregoing provisions would cause us irreparable harm, and we will be entitled to equitable relief, including injunctive relief and specific performance, to enforce the foregoing provisions. Nothing in our current certificate of incorporation or bylaws or our amended and restated certificate of incorporation or amended and restated bylaws precludes stockholders that assert claims under the Exchange Act, from bringing such claims in federal court to the extent that the Exchange Act confers exclusive federal jurisdiction over such claims, subject to applicable law.
paras.zh: 我们修订并重述的公司章程以及修订并重述的公司细则将于本次发行完成前立即生效，其中规定：(i) 除非我们书面同意选择替代法院，否则在法律允许的最大范围内，特拉华州衡平法院（或若该法院不具有标的管辖权，则为特拉华州联邦地区法院）将是以下事项的唯一且专属法院：(A) 代表公司提起的任何派生诉讼或程序，(B) 任何主张基于或依据我们现任或前任董事、高级管理人员、其他员工、代理人或股东对公司或我们的股东所负信托义务之违反的索赔的诉讼，包括但不限于主张协助和教唆该等违反信托义务的索赔，(C) 任何依据《特拉华州普通公司法》任何条款或我们的公司章程或细则对公司或我们现任或前任董事、高级管理人员、员工、代理人或股东提出索赔的诉讼，或《特拉华州普通公司法》赋予特拉华州衡平法院管辖权的诉讼，或 (D) 任何主张与公司相关或涉及公司且受内部事务原则管辖的索赔的诉讼；(ii) 除非我们书面同意选择替代法院，否则在法律允许的最大范围内，美国联邦地区法院将是解决任何依据《证券法》及其下颁布的规则和法规提出的诉讼请求的唯一且专属法院；(iii) 任何购买或以其他方式取得或持有公司股本股份任何权益的个人或实体将被视为已注意到并同意这些规定；以及 (iv) 未能执行上述规定将对我们造成不可弥补的损害，我们将有权获得衡平法救济，包括禁令救济和具体履行，以执行上述规定。我们当前的公司章程或细则或我们修订并重述的公司章程或修订并重述的公司细则中的任何内容，均不妨碍依据《交易法》提出索赔的股东在《交易法》赋予该等索赔专属联邦管辖权的情况下（受适用法律约束）向联邦法院提出该等索赔。

paras.en: The choice of forum provisions may limit a stockholder’s ability to bring a claim in a judicial forum that it finds favorable for disputes with us or any of our current or former directors, officers, other employees, agents, or stockholders, which may discourage such claims against us or any of our current or former directors, officers, other employees, agents, or stockholders and result in increased costs for investors to bring a claim.

paras.en: The principal purposes of this offering are to obtain additional capital to fund our operations, create a public market for our Class A common stock, facilitate our future access to the public equity markets, and increase awareness of our company among potential partners and employees. We currently intend to use the net proceeds from this offering, together with our existing cash, cash equivalents, and investments, for general corporate purposes, including working capital, operating expenses and capital expenditures. We may also use a portion of the net proceeds to in-license, acquire, or invest in complementary technologies, assets, businesses, or intellectual property. We periodically evaluate strategic opportunities; however, we have no current commitments to enter into any such acquisitions or make any such investments.
paras.zh: 本次发行的主要目的是获取额外资本以支持我们的运营、为我们的 A 类普通股建立公开市场、便利我们未来进入公开股权市场，并提高潜在合作伙伴和员工对我们公司的认知度。我们目前拟将本次发行的净收益连同我们现有的现金、现金等价物和投资用于一般公司用途，包括营运资金、经营费用和资本支出。我们也可能将部分净收益用于引进许可、收购或投资于互补性技术、资产、业务或知识产权。我们会定期评估战略机会；但是，我们目前并无任何承诺进行任何此类收购或作出任何此类投资。

paras.en: We intend to use a portion of the net proceeds from this offering to satisfy tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the RSU Net Settlement. Based on the initial public offering price of $185.00 per share of Class A common stock, an estimated 4,799,565 shares underlying RSUs vesting in connection with our initial public offering, and individual tax withholding elections, we will use approximately $416.1 million to satisfy our tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the vesting of such RSUs.
paras.zh: 我们拟将本次发行净收益的一部分用于履行与 RSU 净额结算相关的代扣代缴和汇缴税款义务。基于每股 A 类普通股 185.00 美元的首次公开发行价格、预计因我们的首次公开发行而归属的 4,799,565 股 RSU 相关股份以及个人代扣代缴税款选择，我们将使用约 416.1 百万美元来履行与此类 RSU 归属相关的代扣代缴和汇缴税款义务。

paras.en: In addition, it is possible that in the future, we will decide to “net settle” additional RSUs upon the applicable vesting date, meaning that we will withhold a portion of the vested shares on the applicable vesting date and use some of the net proceeds from this offering to satisfy tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the vesting and settlement of such awards.
paras.zh: 此外，未来我们有可能决定在适用的归属日对额外的 RSU 进行“净额结算”，即我们将在适用的归属日扣留一部分已归属股份，并使用本次发行净收益中的一部分来履行与此类奖励的归属和结算相关的代扣代缴和汇缴税款义务。

paras.en: The expected use of net proceeds from this offering represents our intentions based upon our present plans and business conditions. We cannot predict with certainty all of the particular uses for the proceeds of this offering or the amounts that we will actually spend on the uses set forth above. Accordingly, our management will have broad discretion in applying the net proceeds of this offering. The timing and amount of our actual expenditures will be based on many factors, including cash flows from operations and the anticipated growth of our business.
paras.zh: 本次发行净收益的预期用途代表了我们基于当前计划和业务状况的意图。我们无法确切预测本次发行收益的所有具体用途或我们实际将用于上述用途的金额。因此，我们的管理层在运用本次发行净收益方面将拥有广泛的自主权。我们实际支出的时间和金额将取决于诸多因素，包括经营活动产生的现金流量和我们业务的预期增长。

paras.en: Pending their use, we intend to invest the net proceeds from this offering in a variety of capital-preservation investments, including short-and intermediate-term investments, interest-bearing investments, investment-grade securities, government securities, and money market funds.
paras.zh: 在收益使用之前，我们拟将本次发行的净收益投资于多种资本保全型投资，包括短期和中期投资、有息投资、投资级证券、政府证券和货币市场基金。

paras.en: We have never declared or paid any cash dividends on our capital stock. We currently intend to retain any future earnings for use in the operation of our business and do not anticipate declaring or paying any cash dividends in the foreseeable future. Any future determination to declare cash dividends will be made at the discretion of our board of directors, subject to applicable laws, and will depend on a number of factors, including our results of operations, financial condition, capital requirements, contractual restrictions, general business conditions, and other factors our board of directors may deem relevant. The Revolving Credit Agreement contains restrictions on our ability to pay cash dividends on our Class A common stock. Our ability to pay dividends may be further restricted by agreements we may enter into in the future.
paras.zh: 我们从未就我们的股本宣布或支付任何现金股息。我们目前拟将任何未来收益留存用于经营业务，且预计在可预见的未来不会宣布或支付任何现金股息。未来是否宣布现金股息将由我们的董事会酌情决定，并须遵守适用法律，且将取决于多项因素，包括我们的经营业绩、财务状况、资本需求、合同限制、一般商业状况以及董事会可能认为相关的其他因素。循环信贷协议对我们就 A 类普通股支付现金股息的能力作出了限制。我们支付股息的能力还可能受到我们未来可能签订的协议的进一步限制。

full.sec: Vesting of Shares Underlying the OpenAI Warrant
full.secZh: OpenAI 认股权证项下股份的归属

paras.en: In December 2025, we issued the OpenAI Warrant to OpenAI in connection with the execution of the MRA. Pursuant to the OpenAI Warrant, OpenAI has the right to purchase up to 33,445,026 shares of our Class N common stock at an exercise price of $0.00001 per share.
paras.zh: 2025 年 12 月，我们与 OpenAI 签署 MRA 的同时，向 OpenAI 发行了 OpenAI 认股权证。根据 OpenAI 认股权证，OpenAI 有权以每股 $0.00001 的行权价购买最多 33,445,026 股我们的 N 类普通股。

paras.en: The shares of Class N common stock underlying the OpenAI Warrant vest and become exercisable upon the occurrence of certain events, as set forth below:
paras.zh: OpenAI 认股权证所对应的 N 类普通股股份在发生下述特定事件时归属并可行使：

paras.en: - 4,459,337 shares vested in January 2026 upon our receipt of the Working Capital Loan;
paras.zh: - 4,459,337 股于 2026 年 1 月在我们收到营运资金贷款时归属；

paras.en: - 5,574,171 shares will vest upon the earlier of (i) the first date that our market capitalization exceeds $40 billion, measured by the product of (a) the number of shares of common stock outstanding (on an as-converted basis for each authorized class or series of our common stock), multiplied by (b) the 30-day volume-weighted average closing price per share of our Class A common stock on Nasdaq, and (ii) receipt by us of certain fee payments from OpenAI under the MRA; and
paras.zh: - 5,574,171 股将在以下两者中较早发生之日归属：(i) 我们的市值首次超过 $40 billion 之日，市值按 (a) 已发行普通股股数（按我们各类或各系列普通股授权股份的转换后基础计算）乘以 (b) 我们 A 类普通股在 Nasdaq 的 30 日成交量加权平均每股收盘价计算，以及 (ii) 我们根据 MRA 收到 OpenAI 支付的若干费用款项之日；以及

paras.en: - 23,411,518 shares in the aggregate will vest in multiple tranches on certain committed delivery dates of compute capacity pursuant to the MRA, including committed delivery dates to be mutually agreed upon for the Additional Capacity (as defined in the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations”), if any.
paras.zh: - 合计 23,411,518 股将根据 MRA 在特定算力容量承诺交付日期分多批归属，包括就额外容量（定义见“管理层对财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析”一节）经双方共同商定的承诺交付日期（如有）。

paras.en: The OpenAI Warrant will only fully vest if OpenAI exercises all options to purchase Additional Capacity under the MRA, such that a total of 2GW of AI inference compute capacity and related services is purchased by OpenAI. See the section titled “Certain Relationships and Related Party Transactions—OpenAI Relationship—OpenAI Warrant” for additional information about the OpenAI Warrant.
paras.zh: 仅当 OpenAI 行使全部额外容量购买选择权，从而使 OpenAI 购买的 AI 推理算力容量及相关服务合计达到 2GW 时，OpenAI 认股权证才会全部归属。有关 OpenAI 认股权证的更多信息，请参见“特定关系及关联方交易——OpenAI 关系——OpenAI 认股权证”一节。

paras.en: If you purchase shares of our Class A common stock in this offering, your ownership interest will be diluted to the extent of the difference between the initial public offering price per share of our Class A common stock in this offering and the pro forma as adjusted net tangible book value per share of our Class A common stock immediately after this offering.
paras.zh: 如果您在本次发行中购买我们的 A 类普通股股份，您的所有权权益将因本次发行中我们 A 类普通股每股首次公开发行价格与本次发行完成后我们 A 类普通股每股备考调整后有形净资产账面价值之间的差额而被稀释。

paras.en: As of December 31, 2025, our historical net tangible book value (deficit) was $(578.7) million, or $(9.99) per share of our Class A common stock. Our historical net tangible book value (deficit) per share represents our total tangible assets less total liabilities and redeemable convertible preferred stock, divided by the aggregate number of shares of our Class A common stock outstanding as of December 31, 2025.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我们的历史有形净资产账面价值（赤字）为$(578.7)百万，即我们 A 类普通股每股$(9.99)。我们的历史每股有形净资产账面价值（赤字）代表我们的有形资产总额减去负债总额和可赎回可转换优先股，再除以截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日我们已发行的 A 类普通股股份总数。

paras.en: Our pro forma net tangible book value as of December 31, 2025 was $938.6 million, or $5.07 per share of Class A common stock. Pro forma net tangible book value per share represents tangible assets, less liabilities, divided by the aggregate number of shares of Class A common stock outstanding, after giving effect to (i) the filing and effectiveness of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation; (ii) the Preferred Stock Conversion; (iii) the Common Stock Reclassification; (iv) the RSU Net Settlement; (v) the increase in accrued expenses and other current liabilities and an equivalent decrease in additional paid-in capital of $416.1 million in connection with the estimated tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the RSU Net Settlement; and (vi) stock-based compensation expense of approximately $150.5 million that we will recognize upon the completion of this offering related to RSUs subject to service-based and liquidity-based vesting conditions for which the service-based vesting condition was satisfied as of December 31, 2025 and for which the liquidity-based vesting condition was satisfied in connection with this offering.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我们的备考有形净资产账面价值为$938.6 百万，即 A 类普通股每股$5.07。每股备考有形净资产账面价值代表有形资产减去负债，再除以已发行的 A 类普通股股份总数，在使以下事项生效后：(i)我们经修订和重述的公司章程的提交和生效；(ii)优先股转换；(iii)普通股重新分类；(iv)RSU 净额结算；(v)与 RSU 净额结算相关的估计税款代扣和汇缴义务所导致的应计费用及其他流动负债增加以及额外实收资本等额减少$416.1 百万；以及(vi)我们将在本次发行完成时确认的约$150.5 百万股权激励费用，该费用与受服务期和流动性归属条件约束的 RSU 相关，这些 RSU 的服务期归属条件截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日已满足，且其流动性归属条件已因本次发行而满足。

paras.en: After giving effect to (i) the pro forma adjustments set forth above, (ii) the sale by us of 30,000,000 shares of our Class A common stock in this offering at the initial public offering price of $185.00 per share, after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses payable by us, and (iii) the use of a portion of the net proceeds from this offering to satisfy the estimated tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the RSU Net Settlement, our pro forma as adjusted net tangible book value as of December 31, 2025 would have been $6,347.1 million, or $29.51 per share. This represents an immediate increase in pro forma net tangible book value to existing stockholders of $24.44 per share and an immediate dilution in pro forma net tangible book value to new investors of $155.49 per share. Dilution per share represents the difference between the price per share to be paid by new investors for the shares of our Class A common stock sold in this offering and the pro forma as adjusted net tangible book value per share immediately after this offering.
paras.zh: 在使以下事项生效后：(i)上述备考调整；(ii)我们以每股$185.00 的首次公开发行价格在本次发行中出售 30,000,000 股 A 类普通股，扣除承销折扣和佣金以及我们应付的估计发行费用；以及(iii)使用本次发行净收益的一部分来履行与 RSU 净额结算相关的估计税款代扣和汇缴义务，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日我们的备考调整后有形净资产账面价值将为$6,347.1 百万，即每股$29.51。这代表现有股东的每股备考有形净资产账面价值立即增加$24.44，新投资者的每股备考有形净资产账面价值立即稀释$155.49。每股稀释代表新投资者就本次发行中出售的我们 A 类普通股股份每股支付的价格与本次发行完成后每股备考调整后有形净资产账面价值之间的差额。

paras.en: We are building the fastest AI infrastructure in the world.
paras.zh: 我们正在打造全球最快的 AI 基础设施。

paras.en: In AI, speed is critical to win. Speed improves user engagement, expands product capabilities, can lower operating costs, and opens new markets. It shortens iteration cycles for engineers, researchers, and professionals across industries, allowing them to be more productive. Speed unlocks new applications and new industries.
paras.zh: 在 AI 领域，速度是制胜的关键。速度可提升用户参与度、扩展产品能力、降低运营成本，并开辟新市场。它缩短了各行业工程师、研究人员和专业人士的迭代周期，使他们能够更高效地工作。速度催生新应用和新产业。

paras.en: Our solutions are built for speed. Cerebras Inference delivers answers up to 15 times faster than leading GPU-based solutions as benchmarked on leading open-source models. These performance breakthroughs are the result of our core innovation: the world’s first and only commercialized wafer-scale processor.
paras.zh: 我们的解决方案专为速度而打造。在领先的开源模型基准测试中，Cerebras Inference 提供的答案速度最高可达领先的基于 GPU 的解决方案的 15 倍。这些性能突破源于我们的核心创新：全球首个也是唯一一个实现商业化的晶圆级处理器。

paras.en: Our customers include hyperscalers, foundation model labs, AI-native and digital native businesses, enterprises, and Sovereign AI initiatives. Our customers use Cerebras solutions to run applications that demand speed, scale, and intelligence. This work includes training and serving large frontier models with near-instant responses, processing massive datasets in real time, and generating full-stack applications in a single step.
paras.zh: 我们的客户包括超大规模云服务商、基础模型实验室、AI 原生及数字原生企业、大型企业以及主权 AI 计划。我们的客户使用 Cerebras 解决方案运行对速度、规模和智能有高要求的应用。这些工作包括以近乎即时的响应训练和服务大型前沿模型、实时处理海量数据集，以及一步生成全栈应用。

paras.en: Once customers adopt fast inference, user expectations for interactivity rise, and engineering teams shift from latency optimizations to other work, making it difficult to return to slower inference.
paras.zh: 一旦客户采用快速推理，用户对交互性的期望便会提高，工程团队也会从延迟优化转向其他工作，从而难以再回到较慢的推理。

paras.en: We deliver our solutions to customers in several different ways. Organizations that require full data and infrastructure control can purchase Cerebras AI supercomputers for on-premises deployments. Customers seeking cloud flexibility can access Cerebras compute through consumption-based models on Cerebras Cloud or through partner clouds. For example, our high-speed inference services are available through partners, including AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Marketplace, IBM watsonx Model Gateway, Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, and Hugging Face, enabling seamless adoption within existing workflows. Beyond providing compute infrastructure, we provide AI services to our customers to co-develop solutions to address their most complex challenges, from training state-of-the-art models to optimizing deployments for each application’s needs, and maintaining and operating their on-premises hardware.
paras.zh: 我们通过多种不同方式向客户交付解决方案。需要完全掌控数据和基础设施的组织可以购买 Cerebras AI 超级计算机进行本地部署。寻求云灵活性的客户可以通过 Cerebras Cloud 上基于用量的模式或通过合作伙伴云获取 Cerebras 算力。例如，我们的高速推理服务可通过合作伙伴获取，包括 AWS Marketplace、Microsoft Marketplace、IBM watsonx Model Gateway、Vercel AI Gateway、OpenRouter 和 Hugging Face，从而能够在现有工作流中无缝采用。除提供算力基础设施外，我们还向客户提供 AI 服务，共同开发解决方案以应对其最复杂的挑战，从训练最先进的模型到针对每个应用需求优化部署，以及维护和运营其本地硬件。

paras.en: Our growth reflects the broader acceleration of AI adoption. Our revenue increased from $24.6 million in 2022 to $78.7 million in 2023 and to $290.3 million in 2024, representing a more than tenfold increase over three years. Our revenue increased to $510.0 million in 2025, representing year-over-year growth of 76%. Our gross margin was 12%, 33%, 42% and 39% in 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. We earned net income of $237.8 million in 2025 and incurred net loss of $481.6 million in 2024. We incurred non-GAAP net loss of $75.7 million in 2025 and $21.8 million in 2024, after excluding the impact of stock-based compensation expense and change in fair value (extinguishment) of forward contract liability from our GAAP net income (loss). For more information and for a reconciliation of non-GAAP net loss to net income (loss), see the section titled “—Non-GAAP Financial Measures.”
paras.zh: 我们的增长反映了 AI 采用的更广泛加速。我们的收入从 2022 年的 $24.6 million 增长至 2023 年的 $78.7 million，并增至 2024 年的 $290.3 million，三年间增长超过十倍。我们的收入在 2025 年增至 $510.0 million，同比增长 76%。我们的毛利率在 2022 年、2023 年、2024 年和 2025 年分别为 12%、33%、42% 和 39%。我们在 2025 年实现净利润 $237.8 million，在 2024 年产生净亏损 $481.6 million。在从我们的 GAAP 净利润（亏损）中剔除股权激励费用以及远期合同负债公允价值变动（清偿）的影响后，我们在 2025 年和 2024 年分别产生非 GAAP 净亏损 $75.7 million 和 $21.8 million。有关更多信息以及非 GAAP 净亏损与净利润（亏损）的对账，请参见标题为“—非 GAAP 财务指标”的章节。

paras.en: We deliver high-performance AI offerings primarily through on-premises hardware and cloud-based solutions. Customers can also use a hybrid approach and train models on premises and then leverage our inference cloud in production, benefiting from flexible capacity that can scale with demand. We use a combination of direct sales and partnerships to address the rapidly growing AI market.
paras.zh: 我们主要通过本地部署硬件和基于云的解决方案提供高性能 AI 产品。客户还可以采用混合方式，在本地训练模型，然后在生产环境中利用我们的推理云，从而受益于可随需求扩展的灵活算力。我们采用直销与合作伙伴相结合的方式，以把握快速增长的 AI 市场。

paras.en: On-Premises Hardware Solutions. We sell our hardware platform to leading organizations who seek maximum security over their data and their AI infrastructure, fulfilling their needs for high-performance AI compute on premises. Each system combines tightly integrated hardware and software and includes a renewable software subscription that provides continuous updates and upgrades.
paras.zh: 本地部署硬件解决方案。我们向寻求对其数据和 AI 基础设施实现最高安全性的领先机构销售硬件平台，满足其在本地部署高性能 AI 算力的需求。每套系统将紧密集成的硬件与软件相结合，并包含可续期的软件订阅，提供持续的更新与升级。

paras.en: Cloud and Other Services. We also provide access to Cerebras high-performance AI compute through Cerebras Cloud as well as through our partner cloud platforms, including AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Marketplace, IBM watsonx Model Gateway, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, and Vercel AI Gateway. These offerings enable customers to utilize the full capabilities of our AI supercomputers without incurring the capital expenditures associated with building or maintaining on-premises infrastructure, and without the operational complexity of assembling and managing training or inference software. Customers can begin to use our cloud resources within minutes.
paras.zh: 云及其他服务。我们还通过 Cerebras Cloud 以及我们的合作伙伴云平台（包括 AWS Marketplace、Microsoft Marketplace、IBM watsonx Model Gateway、OpenRouter、Hugging Face 和 Vercel AI Gateway）提供对 Cerebras 高性能 AI 算力的访问。这些产品使客户能够充分利用我们 AI 超级计算机的全部能力，而无需承担构建或维护本地基础设施相关的资本支出，也无需承担组装和管理训练或推理软件的运营复杂性。客户可以在几分钟内开始使用我们的云资源。

paras.en: Cerebras Cloud serves a broad spectrum of users—from individual developers using our entry-level tier to some of the world’s largest enterprises. Customers can run open-source, fine-tuned, and proprietary models for both training and inference workloads. Across a variety of use cases, our cloud offerings provide access to ultra-high-performance AI compute. Customers can procure cloud capacity directly from Cerebras through two primary models: Dedicated Capacity and On-Demand. They can also purchase from our cloud partners.
paras.zh: Cerebras Cloud 服务于广泛的用户群体——从使用我们入门级套餐的个体开发者到全球一些最大的企业。客户可以运行开源、微调和专有模型，用于训练和推理工作负载。在各种用例中，我们的云产品提供对超高性能 AI 算力的访问。客户可以通过两种主要模式直接从 Cerebras 采购云容量：专用容量和按需。他们也可以从我们的云合作伙伴处购买。

paras.en: Our Dedicated Capacity customers receive a single integrated solution tailored to their needs, which is delivered over the contractual term for a predetermined amount of capacity regardless of usage. As such, revenue is recognized over time as these services are provided. For customers seeking compute capacity On-Demand, we sell high-performance AI compute through Cerebras Cloud or our cloud partners, based on various consumption-or usage-based pricing models.
paras.zh: 我们的专用容量客户获得根据其需求定制的单一集成解决方案，该方案在合同期限内以预先确定的容量提供，无论实际使用量如何。因此，收入在这些服务提供的过程中随时间确认。对于寻求按需算力容量的客户，我们通过 Cerebras Cloud 或我们的云合作伙伴销售高性能 AI 算力，基于各种按消费或按使用量计价的定价模式。

paras.en: We also offer deployment services to assist customers with data preparation, model architecture design, training management, inference optimization, and, in select cases, ongoing system operations and management. We also offer a subscription service providing access to an ongoing stream of software updates and upgrades for purchasers of our hardware. We provide professional services to assist customers throughout the entire AI workflow.
paras.zh: 我们还提供部署服务，协助客户进行数据准备、模型架构设计、训练管理、推理优化，并在特定情况下提供持续的系统运营和管理。我们还提供订阅服务，为我们的硬件购买者提供持续的软件更新和升级流。我们提供专业服务，在整个人工智能工作流程中为客户提供协助。

paras.en: #### OpenAI Collaboration
paras.zh: #### OpenAI 合作

paras.en: In December 2025, we entered into a Master Relationship Agreement (the “MRA”) with OpenAI OpCo, LLC (“OpenAI”), under which OpenAI agreed to purchase 750MW of AI inference compute capacity (the “Committed Capacity”) and related services, including collaboration on engineering development and integrations. The relationship is intended to integrate purpose‑built, low‑latency inference systems into OpenAI’s broader compute portfolio, enabling faster response times for complex AI workloads by reducing bottlenecks associated with conventional inference architectures. We expect to deploy the Committed Capacity in tranches during 2026 through 2028, with each tranche of deployed capacity having a term of three or four years that is extendable by OpenAI to a maximum of five years in total. In addition to the Committed Capacity, which we are contractually obligated to deliver and OpenAI is contractually obligated to purchase, OpenAI has the option to purchase an additional 1.25GW of AI inference compute capacity (the “Additional Capacity”) for deployment in tranches by the end of 2030.
paras.zh: 2025 年 12 月，我们与 OpenAI OpCo, LLC（简称“OpenAI”）签订了主关系协议（简称“MRA”），根据该协议，OpenAI 同意购买 750MW 的 AI 推理算力容量（简称“承诺容量”）及相关服务，包括在工程开发和集成方面的合作。该合作关系旨在将专为低延迟推理打造的系统整合进 OpenAI 更广泛的算力组合中，通过减少与传统推理架构相关的瓶颈，为复杂的 AI 工作负载实现更快的响应时间。我们预计将在 2026 年至 2028 年期间分批部署承诺容量，每批已部署容量的期限为三年或四年，OpenAI 可将其延长至总计最长五年。除承诺容量（我们有合同义务交付，OpenAI 有合同义务购买）外，OpenAI 还可选择购买额外 1.25GW 的 AI 推理算力容量（简称“额外容量”），在 2030 年底前分批部署。

paras.en: Pursuant to the MRA, OpenAI is obligated to pay fees to us as capacity tranches are delivered, as well as to reimburse certain data center–related costs as pass-throughs under agreed terms. In addition, to accelerate our engineering development, manufacturing scale up and data center expansion, OpenAI advanced to us a working capital loan of approximately $1.0 billion (the “Working Capital Loan”), which we will repay in cash or through the delivery of compute capacity or hardware or other services under the MRA. The Working Capital Loan is subject to a secured promissory note with a maturity date of no later than December 31, 2032, which may be prepaid in whole or in part at any time without penalty, and which bears interest at 6% per annum, provided any accrued interest shall be waived to the extent such loan is repaid through delivery of compute capacity, hardware or other services, or assignment or transfer of certain assets, in accordance with the MRA.
paras.zh: 根据 MRA,OpenAI 有义务在容量批次交付时向我们支付费用，并按约定条款报销某些数据中心相关成本作为转付费用。此外，为加速我们的工程开发、制造规模扩大和数据中心扩建，OpenAI 向我们提供了约 $1.0 billion 的营运资金贷款（简称“营运资金贷款”），我们将以现金或通过根据 MRA 交付算力容量或硬件或其他服务的方式偿还。该营运资金贷款由一份到期日不迟于 2032 年 12 月 31 日的担保本票作为凭证，可随时全部或部分提前偿还且无需支付罚金，年利率为 6%，但若该贷款通过根据 MRA 交付算力容量、硬件或其他服务，或转让或转移某些资产的方式偿还，则任何应计利息应予豁免。

paras.en: In December 2025, we issued the OpenAI Warrant to OpenAI in connection with the execution of the MRA. Pursuant to the OpenAI Warrant, OpenAI has the right to purchase up to 33,445,026 shares of our Class N common stock at an exercise price of $0.00001 per share. The OpenAI Warrant expires on the earlier of December 24, 2035 and five business days following the first date during which there is no binding capacity purchase commitments or contractually obligated current or future payments under the MRA. The shares of Class N common stock underlying the OpenAI Warrant vest upon the achievement of certain commercial and market capitalization milestones, with full vesting occurring only if OpenAI exercises all options to purchase Additional Capacity under the MRA, such that a total of 2GW of AI inference compute capacity and related services is purchased by OpenAI. See the section titled “Capitalization—Vesting of Shares Underlying the OpenAI Warrant” for additional information.
paras.zh: 2025 年 12 月，我们与 MRA 的签署相关向 OpenAI 发行了 OpenAI 认股权证。根据 OpenAI 认股权证，OpenAI 有权以每股 $0.00001 的行权价购买最多 33,445,026 股我们的 N 类普通股。OpenAI 认股权证于 2035 年 12 月 24 日与 MRA 项下不存在有约束力的容量购买承诺或合同义务的当前或未来付款的首日之后的五个工作日两者中较早者到期。OpenAI 认股权证对应的 N 类普通股在实现某些商业和市值里程碑时归属，仅在 OpenAI 行使 MRA 项下购买额外容量的全部选择权，从而使 OpenAI 购买的 AI 推理算力容量及相关服务总计达到 2GW 时才完全归属。更多信息请参见标题为“资本化——OpenAI 认股权证对应股份的归属”的章节。

paras.en: #### Sovereign AI Initiatives
paras.zh: #### 主权 AI 计划

paras.en: The United Arab Emirates (“UAE”) has emerged as a global leader in AI through its visionary UAE Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 and Vision 2031, which aim to position the nation as a hub for innovation and sustainable development. Spearheaded by the UAE Artificial Intelligence Office, the initiative emphasizes leveraging AI to enhance governance, improve quality of life, and drive economic diversification by integrating AI into key sectors such as healthcare, education, energy, and public services. The UAE has also prioritized building a skilled workforce and contributing to research and development in AI. These efforts align with the broader goal of transforming the UAE into a knowledge-based economy, where AI drives efficiency, innovation, and global competitiveness while addressing societal challenges such as healthcare access and environmental sustainability.
paras.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国（以下简称“阿联酋”）凭借其富有远见的《阿联酋 2031 年人工智能战略》和《2031 年愿景》，已成为全球人工智能领域的领导者，这两项战略旨在将该国打造为创新与可持续发展的中心。该倡议由阿联酋人工智能办公室牵头，强调利用人工智能加强治理、提升生活质量，并通过将人工智能融入医疗健康、教育、能源和公共服务等关键领域来推动经济多元化。阿联酋还优先重视建设高技能劳动力队伍，并为人工智能领域的研发作出贡献。这些努力与将阿联酋转变为知识型经济体的更广泛目标相一致，在这一经济体中，人工智能在应对医疗健康可及性和环境可持续性等社会挑战的同时，推动效率提升、创新和全球竞争力。

paras.en: We have established strategic relationships with Group 42 Holding Ltd (together with its affiliates, “G42”), an Abu Dhabi-based technology group whose portfolio of companies spans multiple sectors such as energy, finance, cloud infrastructure, security, and healthcare; and the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (“MBZUAI”), an Abu Dhabi-based university dedicated entirely to the advancement of science through AI. G42 and MBZUAI have acted as our customers, vendors, partners, and/or research collaborators on multiple initiatives in model training, inference, and AI compute infrastructure.
paras.zh: 我们已与 Group 42 Holding Ltd（连同其关联方，合称“G42”）以及穆罕默德·本·扎耶德人工智能大学（以下简称“MBZUAI”）建立了战略关系。G42 是一家总部位于阿布扎比的技术集团，其旗下公司组合横跨能源、金融、云基础设施、安全和医疗健康等多个领域；MBZUAI 是一所总部位于阿布扎比的大学，完全致力于通过人工智能推动科学进步。G42 和 MBZUAI 在模型训练、推理和人工智能算力基础设施等多项举措中，曾作为我们的客户、供应商、合作伙伴和/或研究合作方。

paras.en: G42 and MBZUAI have been significant customers. For the year ended December 31, 2025, MBZUAI accounted for 62% of our total revenue. G42 accounted for 24% and 85% of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
paras.zh: G42 和 MBZUAI 一直是重要客户。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，MBZUAI 占我们总收入的 62%。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度，G42 分别占我们总收入的 24% 和 85%。

paras.en: In December 2025, we issued a warrant to G42 to purchase an aggregate of up to 1,857,516 shares of our Class N common stock, with an exercise price of $0.01 per share. The warrant is fully vested and was exercised in full in January 2026.
paras.zh: 2025 年 12 月，我们向 G42 发行了一份认股权证，可购买合计最多 1,857,516 股我们的 N 类普通股，行权价为每股 $0.01。该认股权证已完全归属，并已于 2026 年 1 月全额行权。

paras.en: In April 2026, we issued a warrant to G42 to purchase an aggregate of up to 1,655,975 shares of our Class N common stock, with an exercise price of $0.01 per share. The warrant is fully vested and was exercised in full in April 2026.
paras.zh: 2026 年 4 月，我们向 G42 发行了一份认股权证，可购买合计最多 1,655,975 股我们的 N 类普通股，行权价为每股 $0.01。该认股权证已完全归属，并已于 2026 年 4 月全额行权。

full.secZh: 影响我们业绩的关键因素

paras.en: We believe that the growth and future success of our business depend on many factors. While these factors present significant opportunities for our business, they also pose important challenges that we will need to address in order to improve our results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们认为，我们业务的增长和未来成功取决于诸多因素。尽管这些因素为我们的业务带来了重大机遇，但也构成了我们必须应对的重要挑战，以改善我们的经营业绩。

paras.en: Commercial relationship with strategic partners. We expect to derive a substantial portion of our revenue from sales of cloud capacity to OpenAI, G42, and MBZUAI. Any changes in these parties’ demand for our solution, whether due to competitive factors, data center availability, changes in their respective business strategy, budgetary constraints, or other reasons could materially impact our financial performance in the future.
paras.zh: 与战略合作伙伴的商业关系。我们预计，我们收入的很大一部分将来自向 OpenAI、G42 和 MBZUAI 销售云容量。这些方对我们解决方案的需求若发生任何变化，无论是由于竞争因素、数据中心可用性、其各自业务战略的变化、预算限制还是其他原因，都可能对我们未来的财务表现产生重大影响。

paras.en: We have received substantial advance payments from G42 and MBZUAI for our AI systems and a $1.0 billion Working Capital Loan from OpenAI to support future installations. Access to such capital has allowed us to reduce our working capital needs and provide access to a significant portion of our initial production volumes to support our ambitious, multi-year AI investment plans.
paras.zh: 我们已收到 G42 和 MBZUAI 就我们的 AI 系统支付的大额预付款，以及 OpenAI 提供的 $1.0 billion 营运资金贷款，以支持未来的部署。获得此类资金使我们得以降低营运资金需求，并提供我们初始产量中相当大一部分的获取渠道，以支持我们雄心勃勃的多年 AI 投资计划。

paras.en: AI compute demand and highly dynamic models and approaches. The escalating global demand for AI training and inference compute, fueled by advancements in LLMs, GenAI, and other AI-powered applications, plays a significant role in the demand for our solutions. We have designed our AI compute platform to address the challenges of accelerating large-scale AI workloads, and our customer base in hyperscalers, foundation model labs, AI-native and digital-native businesses, and research and government sectors reflects the increasing recognition of our differentiated technology. We believe that increasingly dynamic and complex AI models and approaches will continue to require substantial computational resources and speed for training and inference, and will support the demand for our low-latency, high-performance AI compute platform. We will depend on continued growth in compute demand to drive our future financial performance.
paras.zh: AI 算力需求以及高度动态的模型和方法。受 LLM、GenAI 及其他 AI 驱动型应用进步的推动，全球对 AI 训练和推理算力的需求不断升级，这对我们解决方案的需求起着重要作用。我们设计 AI 算力平台旨在应对加速大规模 AI 工作负载的挑战，我们在超大规模云服务商、基础模型实验室、AI 原生和数字原生企业以及研究和政府部门中的客户群，反映出市场对我们差异化技术的日益认可。我们认为，日益动态和复杂的 AI 模型和方法将继续需要大量计算资源和速度来进行训练和推理，并将支撑对我们低延迟、高性能 AI 算力平台的需求。我们将依赖算力需求的持续增长来推动我们未来的财务表现。

paras.en: Investment in data center capacity. A key determinant of our significant growth in cloud-based solutions will be our ability to continue expanding our cloud infrastructure through the successful procurement of long-term data center arrangements in strategic locations. We need to scale through identifying, negotiating and maintaining long-term data center leases on favorable terms for both power and space to keep pace with demand, including time-based milestones and performance obligations that need to be met for take-or-pay capacity commitments pursuant to the MRA with OpenAI. As we expand our cloud services with OpenAI and other strategic partners through Cerebras Cloud or our cloud partners, we will incur significantly greater capital expenditures. In addition, our operations are further dependent on our professional team’s ability to procure and deploy auxiliary equipment, including cooling systems and back-up generators. Our continued execution in these key areas among others will strengthen our ability to meet customer demand, support expansion, and enhance our overall cloud offering.
paras.zh: 对数据中心容量的投资。我们云解决方案显著增长的一个关键决定因素，将是我们能否通过在战略地点成功采购长期数据中心安排来持续扩展我们的云基础设施。我们需要通过识别、谈判并维持条款有利的长期数据中心租约（涵盖电力和空间两方面）来实现规模扩张，以跟上需求，包括根据与 OpenAI 的 MRA 就照付不议容量承诺所需满足的基于时间的里程碑和履约义务。随着我们通过 Cerebras Cloud 或我们的云合作伙伴扩展与 OpenAI 及其他战略合作伙伴的云服务，我们将产生显著更大的资本支出。此外，我们的运营还进一步依赖于我们专业团队采购和部署辅助设备（包括冷却系统和备用发电机）的能力。我们在这些关键领域及其他方面的持续执行，将增强我们满足客户需求、支持扩张并提升我们整体云产品的能力。

paras.en: Supply chain and manufacturing capacity. We operate a fabless business model that utilizes third-party suppliers and manufacturers, such as third-party wafer foundries and module assembly and test service providers in a number of countries, including outside the United States. We do not generally have long-term capacity commitments with our suppliers, and we source a number of the components used in our products from sole or single-source suppliers or use a single supplier to perform certain of the processes involved in the manufacture of our products. The continued and timely supply of input materials and the availability of manufacturing capacity and packaging and testing services impact our ability to meet customer demand. Onboarding new third-party suppliers and our dependency on them to allocate sufficient manufacturing capacity to meet our needs in a cost-effective and timely manner may impact our ability to scale and support growing customer demand.
paras.zh: 供应链与制造产能。我们采用无晶圆厂经营模式，依托第三方供应商和制造商，例如位于多个国家（包括美国境外）的第三方晶圆代工厂以及模块组装与测试服务提供商。我们通常不与供应商签订长期产能承诺，并且我们的产品中使用的若干组件来自独家或单一来源供应商，或使用单一供应商执行我们产品制造过程中涉及的某些工序。投入材料的持续及时供应以及制造产能和封装测试服务的可获得性，会影响我们满足客户需求的能力。引入新的第三方供应商，以及我们依赖其以具有成本效益且及时的方式分配足够制造产能来满足我们的需求，可能会影响我们扩大规模和支持不断增长的客户需求的能力。

paras.en: New customer adoption. Attracting new customers to our platform is a key driver of our revenue growth strategy. We have successfully grown our customer base to include hyperscalers, foundation model labs, AI-native and digital-native businesses, enterprises, and Sovereign AI initiatives seeking to leverage the power of AI for their specific needs. An increase in new customers will impact our revenue growth and market share and also contributes to a diversified customer base, which can provide greater stability over the long term. Additionally, new customers bring fresh perspectives and use cases, which can drive innovation and product development, further enhancing our competitive position.
paras.zh: 新客户获取。吸引新客户使用我们的平台是我们收入增长战略的关键驱动因素。我们已成功扩大客户群，涵盖超大规模云服务商、基础模型实验室、AI 原生和数字原生企业、企业客户，以及寻求利用 AI 力量满足其特定需求的主权 AI 计划。新客户的增加将影响我们的收入增长和市场份额，也有助于形成多元化的客户群，从而在长期内提供更大的稳定性。此外，新客户带来新的视角和用例，可推动创新和产品开发，进一步增强我们的竞争地位。

paras.en: AI adoption and the emergence of new use cases and applications. We expect to benefit from the rapid adoption of AI across industries and the emergence of innovative AI use cases and applications. As organizations increasingly recognize the transformative potential of AI to enhance efficiency, productivity, and decision-making, we expect the demand for high-performance AI compute solutions to accelerate. The rapidly expanding range of AI use cases, from natural language processing and computer vision to drug discovery and climate modeling, among others, creates a broad market opportunity for our AI compute solution. We expect our ability to address the evolving needs of diverse industries and applications with cutting-edge AI compute technology to be instrumental in driving our growth and market leadership in the years to come.
paras.zh: AI 采用以及新用例和应用的出现。我们预计将受益于 AI 在各行业的快速采用以及创新性 AI 用例和应用的出现。随着各组织日益认识到 AI 在提升效率、生产力和决策方面的变革潜力，我们预计对高性能 AI 算力解决方案的需求将加速增长。从自然语言处理和计算机视觉到药物发现和气候建模等，AI 用例范围迅速扩大，为我们的 AI 算力解决方案创造了广阔的市场机会。我们预计，凭借前沿 AI 算力技术满足各行业和应用不断演变需求的能力，将在未来数年对推动我们的增长和市场领导地位发挥关键作用。

paras.en: Sovereign AI initiatives. The expansion of Sovereign AI initiatives represents a significant opportunity to drive demand for our solution. We believe that our focus on developing secure, high-performance AI infrastructure positions us well to meet this demand. We will invest in our product capabilities as well as sales and marketing initiatives to pursue these opportunities.
paras.zh: 主权 AI 计划。主权 AI 计划的扩张代表着推动我们解决方案需求的重大机遇。我们相信，我们对开发安全、高性能 AI 基础设施的专注使我们处于有利地位，能够满足这一需求。我们将投资于产品能力以及销售和营销举措，以把握这些机遇。

paras.en: Investment in technology leadership and product development. Increasing our investment in technology leadership and product development directly impacts our competitive position and future financial performance. Our continued commitment to research and development enables us to focus on emerging market needs and expand into new applications of AI. As we develop new products and services tailored to specific industries and use cases, we can unlock additional demand and continue to broaden our customer base. Additionally, technical leadership is important to help us attract and retain top talent, which is essential for maintaining our technological edge and driving continuous innovation. A talented workforce, in turn, contributes to the development of new solutions that can continue to fuel our revenue growth. We intend to continue to invest heavily in our research and development efforts to remain competitive.
paras.zh: 对技术领先地位和产品开发的投入。加大对技术领先地位和产品开发的投入，直接影响我们的竞争地位和未来财务业绩。我们对研发的持续承诺使我们能够聚焦新兴市场需求，并拓展至 AI 的新应用领域。随着我们针对特定行业和用例开发新的产品与服务，我们能够释放额外需求并持续扩大客户群。此外，技术领先对于帮助我们吸引和留住顶尖人才至关重要，而这对于保持我们的技术优势和推动持续创新不可或缺。反过来，优秀的人才队伍也有助于开发新解决方案，从而持续推动我们的收入增长。我们打算继续在研发工作上大力投入，以保持竞争力。

paras.en: We use certain non-GAAP financial measures to supplement the performance measures in our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in accordance with GAAP. These non-GAAP financial measures include non-GAAP operating loss and non-GAAP net loss. We use these non-GAAP financial measures for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to assist us in evaluating period-to-period comparisons. By excluding certain items that may not be indicative of our recurring core operating results, we believe that non-GAAP operating loss and non-GAAP net loss provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance. Accordingly, we believe these non-GAAP financial measures are useful to investors and others because they allow for additional information with respect to financial measures used by management in its financial and operational decision-making and they may be used by our institutional investors and the analyst community to help them analyze the health of our business. However, there are a number of limitations related to the use of non-GAAP financial measures, and these non-GAAP measures should be considered in addition to, not as a substitute for or in isolation from, our financial results prepared in accordance with GAAP. Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate these non-GAAP financial measures differently or not at all, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures.
paras.zh: 我们使用某些非 GAAP 财务指标来补充我们合并财务报表中的业绩指标，该等合并财务报表按照 GAAP 列报。该等非 GAAP 财务指标包括非 GAAP 经营亏损和非 GAAP 净亏损。我们将该等非 GAAP 财务指标用于财务和经营决策，并作为协助我们评估各期间比较的工具。通过剔除某些可能无法反映我们经常性核心经营业绩的项目，我们认为非 GAAP 经营亏损和非 GAAP 净亏损提供了有关我们业绩的有意义的补充信息。因此，我们认为该等非 GAAP 财务指标对投资者和其他人士有用，因为它们提供了有关管理层在其财务和经营决策中所使用财务指标的额外信息，并且我们的机构投资者和分析师群体可能会使用该等指标来帮助他们分析我们业务的健康状况。然而，使用非 GAAP 财务指标存在诸多局限性，该等非 GAAP 指标应与我们按照 GAAP 编制的财务业绩一并考虑，而不应作为其替代或孤立于其使用。其他公司（包括我们行业内的公司）对这些非 GAAP 财务指标的计算方式可能不同，或可能根本不计算，这降低了其作为比较指标的实用性。

paras.en: #### Non-GAAP Operating Loss
paras.zh: #### 非 GAAP 经营亏损

paras.en: We define non-GAAP operating loss as operating loss presented in accordance with GAAP, adjusted to exclude stock-based compensation expenses. We have presented non-GAAP operating loss because we consider non-GAAP operating loss to be a useful metric for investors and other users of our financial information in evaluating our operating performance. We exclude the impact of stock-based compensation, a non-cash charge that can vary from period to period, as such variations are unrelated to our core operating performance. This metric also provides investors and other users of our financial information with an additional tool to compare business performance across companies and periods, while eliminating the effects of items that may vary for different companies for reasons unrelated to core operating performance.
paras.zh: 我们将非 GAAP 经营亏损定义为按照 GAAP 列报的经营亏损，并调整以剔除股权激励费用。我们列报非 GAAP 经营亏损，是因为我们认为非 GAAP 经营亏损对于投资者和我们财务信息的其他使用者而言，是评估我们经营业绩的有用指标。我们剔除股权激励的影响，该项非现金费用可能因期间不同而有所变化，因为此类变化与我们的核心经营业绩无关。该指标还为投资者和我们财务信息的其他使用者提供了一项额外工具，用于跨公司和跨期间比较业务业绩，同时消除可能因与核心经营业绩无关的原因而在不同公司之间存在差异的项目的影响。

#### Non-GAAP Net Loss
paras.zh: #### 非 GAAP 净亏损

paras.en: We monitor non-GAAP net loss for planning and performance measurement purposes. We define non-GAAP net loss as net loss reported on our consolidated statements of operations, excluding the impact of stock-based compensation expenses and change in fair value of forward contract liability. We have presented non-GAAP net loss because we believe that the exclusion of these charges allows for a more relevant comparison of our results of operations to other companies in our industry and facilitates period-to-period comparisons as it eliminates the effect of certain factors unrelated to our overall operating performance. Our calculation of non-GAAP net loss does not currently include the tax effects of the stock-based compensation expense adjustment because such tax effects have not been material to date.
paras.zh: 我们出于规划和业绩衡量的目的监控非 GAAP 净亏损。我们将非 GAAP 净亏损定义为我们合并经营报表中所报告的净亏损，但不包括股权激励费用以及远期合同负债公允价值变动的影响。我们列示非 GAAP 净亏损，是因为我们认为剔除这些费用能够使我们的经营业绩与同行业其他公司进行更具相关性的比较，并且由于消除了与我们的整体经营业绩无关的某些因素的影响，有助于进行期间之间的比较。我们目前对非 GAAP 净亏损的计算未包含股权激励费用调整的税务影响，因为该等税务影响迄今为止并不重大。
