paras.en: #### Revenue

We generate revenue primarily from the sale of AI systems, cloud-based offerings, and support services, including custom AI model services. We primarily sell directly to end customers. Contracts with our customers typically include multiple performance obligations. For contracts with more than one performance obligation, we allocate the transaction price to each separate obligation.
paras.zh: 我们的收入主要来自 AI 系统、云端产品及支持服务的销售，包括定制 AI 模型服务。我们主要直接向终端客户销售。与客户的合同通常包含多项履约义务。对于包含一项以上履约义务的合同，我们将交易价格分摊至各项单独履约义务。

paras.en: Hardware Solutions
paras.zh: 硬件解决方案

paras.en: Hardware revenue consists of sales of our AI systems and other equipment that can be used for both training and inference on premise at a customer location. We recognize revenue from sales of AI systems when control of the goods transfers to the customer, which generally occurs upon shipment or delivery, depending on shipping terms or upon meeting the contractual acceptance terms. Beginning in the first quarter of 2026, we expect to recognize non-cash contra-revenue amounts related to the amortization of the value of warrants granted to customers. This is expected to negatively impact sequential revenue growth trends in the near term. Non-cash contra-revenue amounts lower the net revenue reported compared to what would have been recognized without such warrants, while the gross revenue amount without contra-revenue is what the customer is invoiced and pays in cash.
paras.zh: 硬件收入包括销售我们的 AI 系统及其他设备，这些设备既可用于训练，也可用于客户本地部署的推理。我们在商品控制权转移至客户时确认 AI 系统销售收入，该时点通常为发货或交付时（取决于运输条款），或在满足合同验收条款时。自 2026 年第一季度起，我们预计将确认与授予客户的认股权证价值摊销相关的非现金收入抵减金额。预计这将在短期内对收入的环比增长趋势产生负面影响。非现金收入抵减金额会降低所报告的净收入，使其低于在无此类认股权证情况下本应确认的金额，而不含收入抵减的毛收入金额即为客户被开票并以现金支付的金额。

paras.en: Cloud and Other Services
paras.zh: 云及其他服务

paras.en: Customers procure cloud capacity from us through two primary models: Dedicated Capacity and On-Demand. Dedicated Capacity contracts are generally structured as take-or-pay commitments, under which customers pay for dedicated compute capacity irrespective of utilization. We recognize revenue from sales of these cloud-based computing services, including hosted inference, over the service term, as the customer benefits from our services throughout the contract period. In the near term, we also expect to begin recognizing revenue for pass through data center costs due to a customer agreement. Beginning in the first quarter of 2026, we expect to recognize non-cash contra-revenue amounts related to the amortization of the value of warrants granted to customers. This is expected to negatively impact sequential revenue growth trends in the near term. Non-cash contra-revenue amounts lower the net revenue reported compared to what would have been recognized without such warrants, while the gross revenue amount without contra-revenue is what the customer is invoiced and pays in cash.
paras.zh: 客户通过两种主要模式向我们采购云容量：专用容量和按需。专用容量合同通常采用照付不议承诺结构，客户无论是否使用均需为专用算力容量付费。我们在服务期内确认此类云计算的销售（包括托管推理）收入，因为客户在整个合同期内持续从我们的服务中获益。短期内，由于一项客户协议，我们还预计将开始就数据中心成本转嫁确认收入。自 2026 年第一季度起，我们预计将确认与授予客户的认股权证价值摊销相关的非现金收入抵减金额。预计这将在短期内对收入的环比增长趋势产生负面影响。非现金收入抵减金额会降低所报告的净收入，使其低于在无此类认股权证情况下本应确认的金额，而不含收入抵减的毛收入金额即为客户被开票并以现金支付的金额。

paras.en: Our On-Demand model includes a consumption-based “pay-as-you-go” approach for inference, allowing customers to either pay for tokens as they consume them or pre-purchase token bundles for fixed amounts that are drawn down over time as the tokens are consumed, as well as for training workloads that run for contracted periods of time. The On-Demand model allows customers to scale elastically and many customers have begun with on-demand usage and transitioned to dedicated capacity as their workloads expand.
paras.zh: 我们的按需模式包括基于用量的推理“按需付费”方式，允许客户在消耗 token 时为其付费，或预先购买固定金额的 token 包，并随着 token 的消耗逐步扣减，同时也适用于在合同约定期限内运行的训练工作负载。按需模式使客户能够弹性扩展，许多客户从按需使用起步，并随着其工作负载的扩大过渡至专用容量。

paras.en: We generate services and support revenue primarily through software support agreements that range from one to five years, as well as offering a comprehensive suite of services to manage and operate Cerebras supercomputer clusters located in our customer’s data centers. Such revenue is recognized ratably over time as the services are provided.
paras.zh: 我们主要通过为期一至五年的软件支持协议产生服务与支持收入，同时提供一整套服务，用于管理和运营位于客户数据中心的 Cerebras 超级计算机集群。此类收入在服务提供期间按比例确认。

paras.en: We also generate revenue from custom AI modeling services over time as services are provided or at a point-in-time upon completion and acceptance by the customer of contract deliverables, depending on the terms of the agreement.
paras.zh: 我们还通过定制 AI 建模服务产生收入，具体取决于协议条款，收入或在服务提供期间按时间确认，或在合同交付物完成并经客户验收时按某一时点确认。

paras.en: As a result of our recently executed MRA with OpenAI for the delivery of the Committed Capacity, we expect cloud and other services revenue to comprise a significantly higher percentage of total revenue in future periods. The mix of hardware and cloud and other services revenue may vary from period to period based on OpenAI’s deployment options and the manner in which they elect to have the Committed Capacity, and any Additional Capacity, delivered by us.
paras.zh: 由于我们近期与 OpenAI 签署了关于交付承诺算力的 MRA，我们预计未来期间云及其他服务收入占总收入的比例将显著提高。硬件收入与云及其他服务收入的构成可能因 OpenAI 的部署选项及其选择由我们交付承诺算力和任何额外算力的方式而因期间而异。

paras.en: #### Cost of Revenue and Gross Profit
paras.zh: #### 收入成本与毛利

paras.en: Hardware Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 硬件收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for hardware consists primarily of the cost of materials, such as wafers processed by third-party foundries, costs associated with packaging, assembly, shipping, logistics, quality assurance, warranty cost, cost of personnel, including salaries, stock-based compensation, and employee benefits, write-down of inventories, and facilities expenses.
paras.zh: 硬件收入成本主要包括材料成本，例如由第三方代工厂加工的晶圆，以及与封装、组装、运输、物流、质量保证、保修相关的成本，人员成本（包括工资、股权激励费用和员工福利），存货跌价，以及设施费用。

paras.en: Cloud and Other Services Cost of Revenue
paras.zh: 云及其他服务收入成本

paras.en: Cost of revenue for cloud-based and other support services revenue primarily consists of data center costs, depreciation or rental of equipment, cost of personnel, including salaries, stock-based compensation, and employee benefits, and facilities expenses. We expect to incur other start-up costs related to expediting the availability of cloud capacity to fulfill the significant increase in near-term demand.
paras.zh: 云及其他支持服务收入的成本主要包括数据中心成本、设备折旧或租赁、人员成本（包括工资、股权激励费用和员工福利）以及设施费用。我们预计将产生与加快云算力可用性相关的其他启动成本，以满足近期需求的大幅增长。

paras.en: Gross Profit and Gross Margin
paras.zh: 毛利与毛利率

paras.en: Gross profit represents revenue less cost of revenue. Gross margin is gross profit expressed as a percentage of revenue. Our gross profit has been, and we expect will continue to be, influenced by several factors, including sales volume and pricing of our products and services, mix of revenue between hardware and cloud and other services, changes in inventory costs, including wafer yield, contract manufacturing and supplier pricing, data center costs, repair and warranty costs, cost of logistics, and personnel costs.
paras.zh: 毛利为收入减去收入成本。毛利率为毛利占收入的百分比。我们的毛利一直受到并将继续受到若干因素的影响，包括我们产品和服务的销量与定价、硬件收入与云及其他服务收入之间的构成、存货成本变动（包括晶圆良率、合同制造和供应商定价）、数据中心成本、维修与保修成本、物流成本以及人员成本。

paras.en: We expect overall gross profit will decrease in absolute dollars in the near term, driven by start-up costs related to expediting the availability of cloud capacity to fulfill the significant increase in near-term demand. Gross margin in the near term is expected to be significantly lower compared to recent periods, and may fluctuate, due to factors such as contra-revenue that will be recognized in future periods in connection with warrants granted to customers that will lower the amount of revenue reported compared to what would have been recognized without such warrants, customer arrangements with pass through amounts for data center costs that will be included in both revenue and cost of revenue and will have a dilutive impact on gross margin, and other start-up costs related to expediting the availability of cloud capacity to fulfill the significant increase in near-term demand. When we begin to recognize contra-revenue amounts from the warrants in the first quarter of 2026, we expect quarterly revenue growth rates will decline from recent trends. In addition, following this offering (and particularly during the quarter in which this offering is completed), gross margin will be impacted by stock-based compensation expense for equity awards for which the liquidity-based vesting condition was satisfied in connection with this offering.
paras.zh: 我们预计，短期内整体毛利润的绝对金额将下降，原因是与加快云算力可用性相关的启动成本，以满足近期需求的大幅增长。短期内毛利率预计将显著低于近期水平，并可能波动，原因包括：与授予客户的认股权证相关的抵减收入将在未来期间确认，从而降低报告收入金额（相较于未授予该等认股权证本应确认的收入）；与客户安排相关的数据中心成本转嫁金额将同时计入收入和收入成本，并对毛利率产生摊薄影响；以及与加快云算力可用性以满足近期需求大幅增长相关的其他启动成本。当我们于 2026 年第一季度开始确认认股权证产生的抵减收入金额时，我们预计季度收入增长率将较近期趋势下降。此外，本次发行完成后（尤其是在本次发行完成的当季），毛利率将受到股权激励费用的影响，该费用涉及因本次发行而满足流动性归属条件的股权奖励。

paras.en: #### Operating Expenses
paras.zh: #### 运营费用

paras.en: Research and Development Expenses
paras.zh: 研发费用

paras.en: Research and development expenses primarily consist of costs incurred in performing research and development activities and include salaries, stock-based compensation, employee benefits, tape-out costs, which include layout services, mask sets, prototype components, system qualification and testing incurred before releasing new system designs into production, shipping, data center costs, depreciation and amortization, professional services fees, cloud computing, and facilities expenses. We expense research and development costs as incurred.
paras.zh: 研发费用主要包括开展研发活动所产生的成本，包括薪酬、股权激励费用、员工福利、流片成本（包括版图服务、掩膜版、原型组件、在将新系统设计投入生产前发生的系统认证和测试）、运输、数据中心成本、折旧和摊销、专业服务费、云计算以及设施费用。研发成本于发生时计入费用。

paras.en: We also expense software development costs, including costs to develop the software component of hardware to be sold, leased, or marketed to external users, before technological feasibility is reached. Technological feasibility is typically reached shortly before the release of such products.
paras.zh: 我们还将软件开发成本（包括在达到技术可行性之前开发拟向外部用户销售、租赁或营销的硬件软件组件所产生的成本）计入费用。技术可行性通常在相关产品发布前不久达到。

paras.en: We expect research and development expenses to increase in absolute dollar terms as we continue to build new innovations with our wafer-scale technology and to remain competitive in the dynamic AI market. Research and development expenses are forecasted to include additional stock-based compensation expense related to equity awards for which the liquidity-based vesting condition was satisfied in connection with this offering.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着我们继续利用晶圆级技术构建新创新并在动态的 AI 市场中保持竞争力，研发费用的绝对金额将增加。研发费用预计将包括与因本次发行而满足流动性归属条件的股权奖励相关的额外股权激励费用。

paras.en: Sales and Marketing Expenses
paras.zh: 销售和营销费用

paras.en: Sales and marketing expenses primarily consist of personnel costs, including salaries, stock-based compensation, employee benefits, public relations costs, tradeshow and other sales event costs, advertising, travel and entertainment costs, costs to provide prospective customers with demonstrations or trials of Cerebras Cloud, and facilities expenses.
paras.zh: 销售和营销费用主要包括人员成本，包括薪酬、股权激励费用、员工福利、公共关系费用、展会和其它销售活动费用、广告、差旅和招待费用、向潜在客户提供 Cerebras Cloud 演示或试用的成本，以及设施费用。

paras.en: We expect sales and marketing expenses to increase in absolute dollar terms as we grow our customer base and brand. We expect to have higher stock-based compensation expense related to equity awards for which the liquidity-based vesting condition was satisfied in connection with this offering.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着客户群和品牌的发展，销售与营销费用按绝对美元金额计算将有所增加。我们预计，与本招股说明书相关的、已满足流动性归属条件的股权奖励将带来更高的股权激励费用。

paras.en: General and Administrative Expenses
paras.zh: 一般及行政费用

paras.en: General and administrative expenses consist primarily of personnel costs, including salaries, stock-based compensation, employee benefits and bonuses related to corporate, finance, legal, information technology and human resource functions, professional services fees, audit and compliance expenses, software subscription costs, travel and related costs, insurance costs, depreciation and amortization, allocation of facilities and other general corporate expenses. We expect to incur additional expenses as a result of operating as a public company, including expenses to comply with the rules and regulations applicable to companies listed on a national securities exchange, expenses related to auditing, compliance, and reporting obligations pursuant to the rules and regulations of the SEC, as well as higher expenses for general and director and officer insurance, investor relations, and professional services.
paras.zh: 一般及行政费用主要包括人员成本，含薪资、股权激励费用、员工福利及奖金（涉及公司、财务、法务、信息技术和人力资源职能），以及专业服务费、审计与合规费用、软件订阅成本、差旅及相关费用、保险费用、折旧与摊销、设施分摊及其他一般公司费用。我们预计，因作为上市公司运营将产生额外费用，包括为遵守适用于在全国性证券交易所上市公司的规则和法规而发生的费用、根据 SEC 规则和法规履行审计、合规及报告义务相关的费用，以及一般及董事与高管保险、投资者关系和专业服务方面更高的费用。

paras.en: We expect general and administrative expenses to increase in absolute dollar terms as we grow the business and have more employees around the world, and incur additional expenses to operate as a public company, including expenses to comply with rules and regulations applicable to companies listed on a securities exchange, expenses related to compliance and reporting obligations in various jurisdictions, and professional services. We expect to have higher stock-based compensation expense related to equity awards for which the liquidity-based vesting condition was satisfied in connection with this offering.
paras.zh: 我们预计，随着业务增长及全球员工人数增加，一般及行政费用按绝对美元金额计算将有所增加，并且作为上市公司运营将产生额外费用，包括为遵守适用于证券交易所上市公司的规则和法规而发生的费用、在各司法管辖区履行合规与报告义务相关的费用以及专业服务费用。我们预计，与本招股说明书相关的、已满足流动性归属条件的股权奖励将带来更高的股权激励费用。

paras.en: #### Other Income (Expense), Net
paras.zh: #### 其他收入（费用）净额

paras.en: Other income (expense), net consists primarily of interest income, dividend income, and the fair value gains and losses arising from the remeasurement or extinguishment of forward contract liability and warrant liability at each reporting date.
paras.zh: 其他收入（费用）净额主要包括利息收入、股息收入，以及因在每个报告日对远期合同负债和认股权证负债进行重新计量或清偿而产生的公允价值利得和损失。

paras.en: #### Income Tax Expense
paras.zh: #### 所得税费用

paras.en: Income tax expense consists of U.S. federal and state income taxes and income taxes in certain foreign jurisdictions in which we conduct business. We maintain a full valuation allowance on our federal and state deferred tax assets as we have concluded that it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be realized. Our effective tax rate is affected by tax rates in foreign jurisdictions and the relative amounts of income we earn in those jurisdictions, as well as non-deductible expenses, such as stock-based compensation, and changes in our valuation allowance.
paras.zh: 所得税费用包括美国联邦和州所得税以及我们开展业务的某些外国司法管辖区的所得税。我们对联邦和州递延所得税资产维持全额估值备抵，因为我们已得出结论，递延所得税资产很可能无法实现。我们的实际税率受外国司法管辖区税率及我们在这些司法管辖区所赚取收入的相对金额、不可扣除费用（如股权激励费用）以及估值备抵变动的影响。

paras.en: Pursuant to the 2016 Plan, our RSUs vest upon the satisfaction of both service-and liquidity-based vesting conditions. The service-based vesting condition for these awards is generally satisfied by rendering continuous service through the applicable vesting period which is generally four years. The liquidity-based vesting condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of an initial public offering, direct listing, or sale of our company. For such RSUs, we recognize stock-based compensation expense using the accelerated attribution method over the requisite service period if it is probable that the performance conditions will be achieved. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, no stock-based compensation expense has been recognized for RSUs as the liquidity events, as described above, was deemed not probable. Refer to Note 14 – Stock-Based Compensation to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion. As of December 31, 2025, 2,901,491 RSUs had met the service-based vesting condition but not the liquidity-based vesting condition. If a liquidity event had occurred as of December 31, 2025, we would have recognized stock-based compensation expense of $150.5 million, and unrecognized stock-based compensation expense related to RSUs for which the service-based vesting condition had not been satisfied as of December 31, 2025 would have been $193.0 million, which would have been recognized over a weighted-average requisite service period of 1.56 years. In the three months ending June 30, 2026, we expect to record a cumulative stock-based compensation expense of $370.9 million, determined using the grant date fair values of the RSUs, for which we expect the service-based vesting condition will be satisfied as of June 30, 2026 and for which the liquidity-based vesting condition was satisfied in connection with this offering. We will record the remaining stock-based compensation expense related to RSUs using the accelerated attribution method over the remaining requisite service period once the liquidity-based vesting condition is satisfied.
paras.zh: 根据 2016 年计划，我们的 RSU 在同时满足服务条件和流动性条件后方可归属。该等奖励的服务归属条件通常通过在适用归属期内提供连续服务来满足，归属期一般为四年。流动性归属条件在首次公开发行、直接上市或本公司出售发生时满足。对于该等 RSU，如果业绩条件很可能达成，我们将在必要服务期内采用加速归属法确认股权激励费用。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度，由于上述流动性事件被视为很可能不会发生，我们未就 RSU 确认任何股权激励费用。进一步讨论请参见本招股说明书其他部分所载经审计合并财务报表附注 14——股权激励。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，2,901,491 份 RSU 已满足服务归属条件但尚未满足流动性归属条件。倘若截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日已发生流动性事件，我们将已确认股权激励费用 $150.5 million，而截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日尚未满足服务归属条件的 RSU 相关的未确认股权激励费用将为 $193.0 million，该费用本应在 1.56 年的加权平均必要服务期内确认。在截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日的三个月内，我们预计将确认累计股权激励费用 $370.9 million，该金额按 RSU 的授予日公允价值确定，我们预计该等 RSU 的服务归属条件将于 2026 年 6 月 30 日满足，且其流动性归属条件已因本次发行而满足。一旦流动性归属条件满足，我们将就 RSU 相关的剩余股权激励费用在剩余必要服务期内采用加速归属法确认。

paras.en: In addition, as described in the section titled “Executive and Director Compensation—Narrative to Summary Compensation Table—Equity-Based Compensation—2026 Founder Equity Awards,” in February 2026, our board of directors granted performance stock units to our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Technology Officer. We are in the process of determining the grant-date fair value of these awards in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 718, Compensation—Stock Compensation. The fair value of the option will be recognized as compensation expense over the requisite service period, using the accelerated attribution method, once the performance condition becomes probable of being achieved. Once the performance condition is met, the compensation expense will be recognized over the requisite service period, regardless of whether, and the extent to which, the market condition is ultimately satisfied.
paras.zh: 此外，如“高管与董事薪酬——薪酬汇总表说明——股权激励——2026 年创始人股权奖励”一节所述，2026 年 2 月，我们的董事会向我们的首席执行官和首席技术官授予了业绩股票单位。我们正在根据会计准则汇编（“ASC”）718《薪酬——股权激励》确定该等奖励的授予日公允价值。一旦业绩条件很可能达成，期权的公允价值将在必要服务期内采用加速归属法确认为薪酬费用。一旦业绩条件达成，薪酬费用将在必要服务期内确认，无论市场条件最终是否满足以及满足程度如何。

paras.en: As of December 31, 2025, our principal sources of liquidity were cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $930.4 million and marketable securities of $406.5 million. Our cash and cash equivalents primarily consisted of cash deposited in money market or holding accounts with financial institutions. Marketable securities were comprised of investments in U.S. government securities with an original maturity greater than three months at the time of purchase but less than or equal to one year at period-end.

paras.en: Since our inception, we have financed our operations primarily through sales of redeemable convertible preferred stock and payments from our customers, including prepayments from G42 and MBZUAI. We had no outstanding debt as of December 31, 2025. Our principal uses of cash in recent periods have been to fund our operations and invest in research and development. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $905.3 million.
paras.zh: 自成立以来，我们主要通过发行可赎回可转换优先股以及来自客户的付款（包括 G42 和 MBZUAI 的预付款）为运营提供资金。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我们无未偿债务。近期我们的主要现金用途为运营资金及研发投入。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我们的累计亏损为 $905.3 million。

paras.en: In January 2026, our capital resources increased significantly when we received an additional $2.0 billion in cash, consisting of $1.0 billion in net proceeds from the issuance of Series H redeemable convertible preferred stock and $1.0 billion from the Working Capital Loan. Refer to Note 18 – Subsequent Events to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion.
paras.zh: 2026 年 1 月，我们的资本资源显著增加，收到额外现金 $2.0 billion，其中包括发行 H 系列可赎回可转换优先股所得净收益 $1.0 billion 以及营运资金贷款 $1.0 billion。有关进一步讨论，请参阅本招股说明书其他部分所载经审计合并财务报表附注 18——期后事项。

paras.en: We believe that our current cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and marketable securities will be sufficient to fund our operations for at least the next 12 months from the date of this prospectus. Our future capital requirements, however, will depend on many factors, including our growth rate, the portion of our business that comes from cloud services requiring additional capital expense for our systems and related long term data center obligations, the timing and extent of our sales and marketing and research and development expenditures including personnel costs, capital expenditures for tape-outs of our chip designs, the continuing market acceptance of our products, and the use of cash to fund potential mergers or acquisitions. In the event that additional financing is required from outside sources, we may seek to raise additional funds through equity, equity-linked arrangements, and debt. The sale of additional equity would result in dilution to our stockholders. The incurrence of debt would result in debt service obligations, and the instruments governing such debt could provide for operational and/or financial covenants that further restrict our operations. If we are unable to raise additional capital when desired and at reasonable rates, our business, results of operations, and financial condition could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们认为，我们现有的现金、现金等价物、受限现金及有价证券足以自本招股说明书日期起至少未来 12 个月内为我们的运营提供资金。然而，我们未来的资本需求将取决于诸多因素，包括我们的增长率、来自云服务的业务占比（该业务需要为我们的系统及相关长期数据中心义务增加资本开支）、我们的销售与营销及研发支出（包括人员成本）的时点和规模、芯片设计流片的资本开支、我们产品的持续市场接受度，以及用于为潜在合并或收购提供资金的现金使用。若需要从外部来源获得额外融资，我们可能寻求通过股权、股权挂钩安排及债务筹集额外资金。额外发行股权将导致我们的股东被稀释。发生债务将导致偿债义务，且管辖该等债务的协议可能规定运营和/或财务契约，从而进一步限制我们的运营。如果我们无法在需要时以合理利率筹集额外资本，我们的业务、经营业绩和财务状况可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: #### Revolving Credit Agreement
paras.zh: #### 循环信贷协议

paras.en: On April 14, 2026, we entered into a revolving credit and guaranty agreement (the “Revolving Credit Agreement”) with Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc., as administrative agent and collateral agent, the letter of credit issuers from time to time party thereto, and the lenders from time to time party thereto, which provides for a revolving credit facility (the “Revolving Credit Facility”) of up to $250.0 million that may initially be used solely for standby letters of credit to data center landlords and developers. Prior to the Phase Two Effective Date (as defined below), loans under the Revolving Credit Facility will incur interest, at our option, at a rate per annum equal to either (i) a base rate or (ii) term secured overnight interest rate (“SOFR”) plus 1.50%. Additionally, prior to the Phase Two Effective Date, we will be required to pay commitment fees of 0.250% per annum on the undrawn portion of the commitments under the Revolving Credit Facility. Prior to the Phase Two Effective Date, the obligations under the Revolving Credit Facility are secured by cash collateral only, with no guarantees required.
paras.zh: 2026 年 4 月 14 日，我们与 Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc.（作为行政代理人和抵押代理人）、不时作为信用证开立方的各方以及不时作为贷款方的各方签订了循环信贷及担保协议（“循环信贷协议”），该协议提供了一项金额最高为$250.0 million 的循环信贷融资（“循环信贷融资”），初始阶段仅可用于向数据中心出租方和开发商开立备用信用证。在第二阶段生效日（定义见下文）之前，循环信贷融资项下的借款将按我们的选择，以等于以下任一利率的年利率计息：(i)基准利率，或(ii)期限有担保隔夜融资利率（"SOFR"）加 1.50%。此外，在第二阶段生效日之前，我们将须就循环信贷融资项下未提取的承诺金额按每年 0.250%支付承诺费。在第二阶段生效日之前，循环信贷融资项下的义务仅以现金抵押品提供担保，无需提供担保。

paras.en: Following the completion of this offering, and on the date we meet pro forma covenant compliance and customary closing conditions (such date, the “Phase Two Effective Date”), the Revolving Credit Facility shall be upsized to up to $850.0 million, the proceeds of which may be used for general corporate purposes. On and after the Phase Two Effective Date, loans under the Revolving Credit Facility will incur interest, at our option, at a rate per annum equal to either (i) a base rate or (ii) term SOFR plus 2.25%, which decreases to 2.00% per annum upon achievement of an enhanced debt to EBITDA ratio. On and after the Phase Two Effective Date, we will be required to pay commitment fees of 0.375% per annum on the undrawn portion of the commitments under the Revolving Credit Facility. The Revolving Credit Facility matures on April 14, 2031. On and after the Phase Two Effective Date, the obligations under the Revolving Credit Facility are secured by liens on substantially all of our assets with carveouts for certain items, including securitization and leased infrastructure assets.
paras.zh: 本次发行完成后，且在我们满足备考契约合规要求及惯常交割条件之日（该日期称为“第二阶段生效日”），循环信贷融资将增额至最高$850.0 million，其所得款项可用于一般公司用途。自第二阶段生效日（含当日）起，循环信贷融资项下的借款将按我们的选择，以等于以下任一利率的年利率计息：(i)基准利率，或(ii)期限 SOFR 加 2.25%，在达到更高的债务与 EBITDA 比率后，该利率将降至每年 2.00%。自第二阶段生效日（含当日）起，我们将须就循环信贷融资项下未提取的承诺金额按每年 0.375%支付承诺费。循环信贷融资于 2031 年 4 月 14 日到期。自第二阶段生效日（含当日）起，循环信贷融资项下的义务以我们几乎全部资产上的留置权提供担保，但某些项目除外，包括证券化资产和租赁基础设施资产。

paras.en: The Revolving Credit Agreement contains a liquidity covenant requiring that unrestricted cash and cash equivalents (subject to certain exclusions), plus the undrawn revolver commitments, be not less than $150.0 million as of the last day of each fiscal quarter. Additionally, the Revolving Credit Agreement contains customary affirmative and, commencing on and after the Phase Two Effective Date, negative covenants (including restrictions on indebtedness, liens, investments, asset dispositions, and affiliate transactions, each subject to customary exceptions and baskets) and customary events of default (including, among other things, non-payment of principal, interest or fees, inaccuracy of representations and warranties, violation of certain covenants, cross-default to certain other indebtedness, bankruptcy and insolvency events, material judgments, change of control, and certain material ERISA events).
paras.zh: 循环信贷协议包含一项流动性契约，要求截至每个财季最后一日，非受限现金及现金等价物（受某些除外项目约束）加上未提取的循环信贷承诺金额不得低于$150.0 million。此外，循环信贷协议包含惯常的肯定性契约，以及自第二阶段生效日（含当日）起适用的否定性契约（包括对债务、留置权、投资、资产处置和关联方交易的限制，各项均受惯常例外和篮子条款约束）和惯常的违约事件（包括但不限于未支付本金、利息或费用，陈述和保证不准确，违反某些契约，对某些其他债务的交叉违约，破产和资不抵债事件，重大判决，控制权变更，以及某些重大 ERISA 事件）。

paras.en: Net cash used in operating activities was $10.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2025. Our largest source of operating cash was cash collection from sales of our products to customers. Net income of $237.8 million, includes a one-time $363.3 million gain due to the extinguishment of the Forward Contract Liability related to the purchase agreement for certain Series F redeemable convertible preferred stock (refer to Note 12 – Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion). Operating cash flows reflect a decrease in customer deposits of $285.9 million as these prepayments offset amounts invoiced for items delivered subject to related purchase orders, as well as an increase to prepaid and other assets of $13.9 million. These decreases to operating cash flows were partially offset by $131.7 million of non-cash charges primarily consisting of stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization expense, non-cash lease expense, and for provision for product warranties. Changes in working capital include increases from deferred revenue $109.5 million as our total revenues increased, a decrease in inventories of $63.3 million as we sold and deployed more product in our data centers, a decrease in accounts receivable $87.0 million due to timing of payments, an increase in accounts payable of $21.2 million related to higher expenses and timing of payments and other liabilities of $3.1 million.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度，经营活动使用的现金净额为$10.0 million。我们经营现金的最大来源是向客户销售产品所收取的现金。净利润$237.8 million 中包含一笔一次性收益$363.3 million，系因与购买协议相关的远期合同负债（涉及某些 F 类可赎回可转换优先股）的清偿而产生（进一步讨论请参见本招股说明书其他部分所载经审计合并财务报表附注 12——可赎回可转换优先股）。经营活动现金流量反映了客户存款减少$285.9 million，原因是这些预付款抵销了就已按相关采购订单交付的项目所开具发票的金额，以及预付款项和其他资产增加$13.9 million。经营活动现金流量的这些减少被$131.7 million 的非现金费用部分抵销，该等费用主要包括股权激励费用、折旧和摊销费用、非现金租赁费用以及产品保修准备。营运资金变动包括：随着总收入增长，递延收入增加$109.5 million；随着我们在数据中心销售和部署更多产品，存货减少$63.3 million；由于付款时间安排，应收账款减少$87.0 million；与费用增加和付款时间安排相关的应付账款增加$21.2 million，以及其他负债增加$3.1 million。

paras.en: Net cash provided by operating activities was $452.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, driven primarily by a $640.3 million increase in customer deposits and a $38.2 million increase in deferred revenue from higher support service sales. These inflows were partially offset by working capital uses, including a $145.0 million increase in inventory due to higher order volumes, a $130.7 million increase in accounts receivable, and a $17.1 million increase in prepaid expenses and other assets, partially mitigated by a $57.7 million increase in accounts payable and other liabilities. Operating cash flows also reflect a net loss of $481.6 million adjusted for non-cash items, including a $401.3 million change in fair value of forward contract liability, $58.6 million of stock-based compensation, $11.5 million of depreciation and amortization, and $25.3 million of other non-cash charges, partially offset by $6.5 million related to amortization of premium and accretion of discount on investments.
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日的年度，经营活动提供的现金净额为$452.0 million，主要受客户存款增加$640.3 million 以及支持服务销售额增长带来的递延收入增加$38.2 million 所推动。这些流入被营运资金使用部分抵销，包括因订单量增加导致存货增加$145.0 million、应收账款增加$130.7 million 以及预付款项和其他资产增加$17.1 million，并被应付账款和其他负债增加$57.7 million 部分缓解。经营活动现金流量还反映了净亏损$481.6 million 经非现金项目调整后的结果，其中包括远期合同负债公允价值变动$401.3 million、股权激励费用$58.6 million、折旧和摊销$11.5 million 以及其他非现金费用$25.3 million，并被与投资溢价摊销和折价增值相关的$6.5 million 部分抵销。

paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度，投资活动所用净现金为 $16.8 million，系由 $23.4 million 的物业及设备购置以及 $302.9 million 的各类投资购置构成，并由 $309.5 million 的该等投资到期及出售所抵减。

paras.zh: #### 融资活动

full.sec: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
full.secZh: 关于市场风险的定量和定性披露

paras.en: #### Foreign Currency and Exchange Risk
paras.zh: #### 外汇与汇率风险

paras.en: The functional currency for each of our subsidiaries, including our subsidiaries located in Canada and India, is the local currency of the country in which the subsidiary operates. As such, we expect to be exposed to both currency transaction remeasurement and translation risk. However, we engage in a small number and immaterial amount of transactions outside of the functional currency of the reporting unit, resulting in negligible exposure to foreign currency risk. We have not hedged such exposure, although we may do so in the future if our exposure to foreign currency risk increases. Any fluctuations in exchange rates may adversely affect our financial position, results of operations and cash flows.
paras.zh: 我们各子公司（包括位于加拿大和印度的子公司）的功能货币为子公司经营所在国家的当地货币。因此，我们预计将面临货币交易重新计量风险和折算风险。然而，我们在报告单位功能货币之外进行的交易数量较少且金额不重大，因此外汇风险敞口极小。我们尚未对此类敞口进行对冲，但若未来外汇风险敞口增加，我们可能会进行对冲。汇率的任何波动均可能对我们的财务状况、经营成果和现金流量产生不利影响。

paras.en: #### Interest Rate Risk
paras.zh: #### 利率风险

paras.en: We had cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $930.4 million as of December 31, 2025. Cash and cash equivalents primarily consists of amounts deposited in money market instruments with financial institutions that have an original maturity of three months or less. We hold cash and cash equivalents for working capital purposes. Due to the short-term nature of our investments, we have not been exposed to, nor do we anticipate being exposed to, material risks due to changes in interest rates. A hypothetical 10% change in interest rates during any of the periods presented would not have had a material impact on our historical consolidated financial statements.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我们的现金、现金等价物及受限现金为 $930.4 million。现金及现金等价物主要包括存放于金融机构、原始到期期限为三个月或以内的货币市场工具中的款项。我们持有现金及现金等价物用于营运资金目的。由于我们投资的短期性质，我们未曾且预计不会因利率变动而面临重大风险。在所呈报的任何期间内，利率发生 10% 的假设性变动不会对我们的历史合并财务报表产生重大影响。

paras.en: We prepare our financial statements in accordance with GAAP. In preparing these financial statements, we are required to make estimates and judgments that affect the amounts and balances reported and contingencies disclosed. We evaluate our estimates on an ongoing basis, specifically including those related to revenue recognition, inventory, stock-based compensation, valuation of our common stock, and income taxes, and base our estimates on historical experience and various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities.
paras.zh: 我们按照 GAAP 编制财务报表。在编制该等财务报表时，我们需要作出影响所报告金额和余额以及所披露或有事项的估计和判断。我们持续评估我们的估计，具体包括与收入确认、存货、股权激励费用、普通股估值和所得税相关的估计，并且我们的估计基于历史经验以及我们认为在相关情况下合理的各项其他假设，这些估计的结果构成对资产和负债账面价值作出判断的基础。

paras.en: The following critical accounting estimates require the use of significant judgment and estimation in the preparation of our audited consolidated financial statements. The accounting estimates and judgment discussed in this section are those that we consider to be the most critical in the preparation of our audited consolidated financial statements. Refer to Note 4 – Significant Accounting Policies to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion.
paras.zh: 以下关键会计估计在编制我们经审计的合并财务报表时需要运用重大判断和估计。本节所讨论的会计估计和判断是我们在编制经审计的合并财务报表时认为最为关键的估计和判断。进一步讨论请参见本招股说明书其他部分所载我们经审计的合并财务报表附注 4——重要会计政策。

paras.en: #### Revenue Recognition
paras.zh: #### 收入确认

paras.en: We derive substantially all of our revenue through sales of hardware, delivery of inference services, and embedded software and through provision of installation, integration, and acceptance services and other technical support to our customers.
paras.zh: 我们的绝大部分收入来自硬件销售、推理服务交付和嵌入式软件，以及向客户提供安装、集成和验收服务及其他技术支持。

paras.en: Contracts with Multiple Performance Obligations
paras.zh: 包含多项履约义务的合同

paras.en: A critical estimate required in recognizing revenue relates to contracts consisting of more than one performance obligation. When a contract with a customer consists of more than one performance obligation, we must exercise judgment in determining whether each obligation within the contract is distinct as well as in determining the relative standalone selling price to allocate to each performance obligation.
paras.zh: 收入确认所需的一项关键估计涉及包含一项以上履约义务的合同。当与客户签订的合同包含一项以上履约义务时，我们必须在判断合同内每项义务是否可明确区分以及确定分摊至每项履约义务的相对单独售价时运用判断。

paras.en: Typically, the standalone selling price is the price at which we sell a promised good or service separately to a customer. The best evidence of the standalone selling price, when available, is the price we have charged for goods or services in similar circumstances and to similar customers. If the standalone selling price is not directly observable, management estimates the standalone selling price using various observable inputs including cost-plus expected margin analysis due to the limited standalone sales history.
paras.zh: 通常，单独售价是我们单独向客户销售某项承诺商品或服务的价格。单独售价的最佳证据（在可获得时）是我们在类似情况下向类似客户收取的商品或服务价格。如果单独售价无法直接观察，管理层使用各项可观察输入值估计单独售价，包括由于单独销售历史有限而采用的成本加成预期利润率分析。

paras.en: Certain arrangements include non-cash consideration, including equity instruments issued to customers, which require judgment in determining the fair value of such instruments, assessing the probability of vesting for instruments subject to performance conditions, and determining the timing of recognition as a reduction of revenue.
paras.zh: 某些安排包含非现金对价，包括向客户发行的权益工具，这需要判断确定该等工具的公允价值、评估受业绩条件约束的工具归属的可能性，以及确定作为收入抵减确认的时点。

paras.en: Refer to Note 4 – Significant Accounting Policies—Revenue Recognition to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion.
paras.zh: 进一步讨论请参见本招股说明书其他部分所载我们经审计的合并财务报表附注 4——重要会计政策——收入确认。

paras.en: #### Stock-Based Compensation
paras.zh: #### 股权激励费用

paras.en: We measure stock-based awards, including stock options, restricted stock unit (“RSUs”), and restricted stock awards (“RSAs”), granted to employees and non-employees based on the estimated fair value as of the grant date. Stock option awards with only service-based vesting conditions are granted to employees and non-employees. The fair value of stock options are estimated using the Black-Scholes option pricing model, which requires the input of highly subjective assumptions, including the fair value of the underlying common stock, the expected term of the stock option, the expected volatility of the price of our common stock, risk-free interest rates, and the expected dividend yield of our common stock. Changes in the assumptions can materially affect the fair value and ultimately how much stock-based compensation expense is recognized. These inputs are subjective and generally require significant analysis and judgment to develop. The fair value of RSUs and RSAs are based on the price of our common stock on the date of grant.
paras.zh: 我们以授予日的估计公允价值为基础，计量授予员工及非员工的股份支付奖励，包括股票期权、限制性股票单位（"RSU"）及限制性股票奖励（"RSA"）。仅附服务期归属条件的股票期权奖励授予员工及非员工。股票期权的公允价值采用 Black-Scholes 期权定价模型估计，该模型需要输入高度主观的假设，包括标的普通股的公允价值、股票期权的预期期限、我们普通股价格的预期波动率、无风险利率以及我们普通股的预期股息率。假设的变化可能对公允价值以及最终确认的股权激励费用金额产生重大影响。这些输入具有主观性，通常需要大量分析和判断才能确定。RSU 和 RSA 的公允价值以授予日我们普通股的价格为基础。

paras.en: We recognize the fair value of each award with only service-based vesting conditions on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period of the award. For certain equity awards that have both service-and liquidity-based vesting conditions, we recognize the expense using the accelerated attribution method over the requisite service period if it is probable that the performance conditions will be achieved. We reassess the achievement of the performance conditions at each reporting date and adjust the stock-based compensation accordingly for such awards. Stock-based compensation expense is based on the value of the portion of stock-based awards that is ultimately expected to vest. As such, our stock-based compensation is reduced for the estimated forfeitures at the date of grant and revised, if necessary, in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates.
paras.zh: 对于仅附服务期归属条件的每项奖励，我们在该奖励的必需服务期内按直线法确认其公允价值。对于同时附服务期和流动性归属条件的某些权益奖励，如果业绩条件很可能达成，我们在必需服务期内采用加速归属法确认费用。我们在每个报告日重新评估业绩条件的达成情况，并对此类奖励的股权激励费用进行相应调整。股权激励费用以最终预计归属的股份支付奖励部分的价值为基础。因此，我们的股权激励费用在授予日扣减估计的没收额，并在后续期间若实际没收额与估计数不同时进行必要修订。

paras.en: Pursuant to the 2016 Plan, our RSUs vest on satisfaction of both service-and liquidity-based vesting conditions. The service-based vesting condition for these awards is generally satisfied by rendering continuous service through the applicable vesting period, which is generally four years. The liquidity-based vesting condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of an initial public offering, direct listing, or sale of our company, given prevailing market conditions. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, no stock-based compensation expense had been recognized, except in connection with RSUs that participated in our tender offer during the year ended December 31, 2025. Refer to Note 14 – Stock-Based Compensation to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion.
paras.zh: 根据 2016 年计划，我们的 RSU 在同时满足服务期和流动性归属条件时归属。此类奖励的服务期归属条件通常通过在适用归属期内持续提供服务而满足，归属期一般为四年。流动性归属条件在发生首次公开发行、直接上市或本公司出售时（视当时市场状况而定）满足。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度，除与截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度参与我们要约收购的 RSU 相关者外，未确认任何股权激励费用。进一步讨论请参阅本招股说明书其他部分所载我们经审计合并财务报表附注 14——股权激励。

paras.en: #### Common Stock Valuations
paras.zh: #### 普通股估值

paras.en: The fair value of common stock underlying our stock-based awards has historically been determined by our board of directors, with input from management and contemporaneous third-party valuations. We believe that our board of directors has the relevant experience and expertise to determine the fair value of our common stock. Given the absence of a public trading market of our common stock, and in accordance with the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants Practice Aid, Valuation of Privately-Held Company Equity Securities Issued as Compensation, our board of directors exercised reasonable judgment and considered numerous objective and subjective factors to determine the best estimate of the fair value of our common stock at each grant date. These factors included:
paras.zh: 我们股权激励奖励所对应普通股的公允价值，历来由董事会根据管理层意见及同期第三方估值确定。我们认为，董事会具备相关经验与专业能力，可确定我们普通股的公允价值。鉴于我们普通股缺乏公开交易市场，且依据美国注册会计师协会《实务指引：作为补偿发行的非上市公司股权证券估值》，董事会在每个授予日行使合理判断，并考虑众多客观和主观因素，以确定对我们普通股公允价值的最佳估计。这些因素包括：

paras.en: - the results of contemporaneous valuations performed at periodic intervals by a third-party valuation firm;
paras.zh: - 第三方估值公司按定期间隔进行的同期估值结果；

paras.en: - the prices, rights, preferences, and privileges of our redeemable convertible preferred stock relative to those of our common stock;
paras.zh: - 我们可赎回可转换优先股相对于普通股的价格、权利、优先权和特权；

paras.en: - the prices of our redeemable convertible preferred stock and common stock sold to investors in arms-length transactions;
paras.zh: - 在公平交易中向投资者出售的可赎回可转换优先股和普通股的价格；

paras.en: - our actual operating and financial performance and estimated trends and prospects for our future performance;
paras.zh: - 我们的实际经营和财务业绩，以及对未来业绩的估计趋势和前景；

paras.en: - our stage of development;
paras.zh: - 我们的发展阶段；

paras.en: - the likelihood of achieving a liquidity event, such as an initial public offering, direct listing, or sale of our company, given prevailing market conditions;
paras.zh: - 鉴于当前市场状况，实现流动性事件（如首次公开发行、直接上市或出售公司）的可能性；

paras.en: - the lack of marketability involving securities in a private company;
paras.zh: - 私人公司证券缺乏市场流通性；

paras.en: - the market performance of comparable publicly traded companies; and
paras.zh: - 可比上市公司的市场表现；以及

paras.en: - U.S. and global capital market conditions.
paras.zh: - 美国和全球资本市场状况。

paras.en: In valuing our common stock, the fair value of our business was determined using various valuation methods, including combinations of the income approach and the market approach with input from management. The income approach involves applying an appropriate risk-adjusted discount rate to projected cash flows based on forecasted revenue and costs. The market approach estimates value based on a comparison of our company to comparable public companies in a similar line of business. From the comparable companies, a representative market value multiple was determined, which was applied to our operating results to estimate the enterprise value of our company.
paras.zh: 在对我们的普通股进行估值时，我们业务的公允价值采用多种估值方法确定，包括结合管理层意见的收入法和市场法的组合。收入法涉及根据预测收入和成本对预计现金流应用适当的风险调整折现率。市场法通过将我们公司与类似业务领域的可比上市公司进行比较来估计价值。从可比公司中确定具有代表性的市场价值倍数，并将其应用于我们的经营业绩，以估计我们公司的企业价值。

paras.en: Once the enterprise value was determined under the market approach, we derived the equity value of our company and used a hybrid method that considered both an option pricing model (“OPM”) and the probability weighted expected return method (“PWERM”) to allocate that value among the various classes of securities to arrive at the fair value of our common stock. The OPM is based on the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model, which allows for the identification for a range of possible future outcomes, each with an associated probability. The OPM is appropriate to use when the range of possible future outcomes is difficult to predict and thus creates highly speculative forecasts. PWERM involves a forward-looking analysis of the possible future outcomes of an enterprise, including an initial public offering as well as non-initial public offering market-based outcomes. After the equity value is determined and allocated to the various classes of securities, a discount for lack of marketability (“DLOM”) is applied to arrive at the fair value of our common stock. A DLOM is applied based on the theory that as an owner of private company stock, the stockholder has limited opportunities to sell this stock, and any such sale would involve significant transaction costs, thereby reducing overall fair market value.
paras.zh: 在市场法下确定企业价值后，我们推导出公司的股权价值，并采用了一种混合方法，该方法同时考虑期权定价模型（"OPM"）和概率加权预期回报法（"PWERM"），将该价值在各类别证券之间进行分配，从而得出我们普通股的公允价值。OPM 基于 Black-Scholes-Merton 期权定价模型，该模型能够识别一系列可能的未来结果，每种结果均附带相应的概率。当可能的未来结果范围难以预测、从而产生高度投机性预测时，采用 OPM 是适当的。PWERM 涉及对企业可能的未来结果进行前瞻性分析，包括首次公开发行以及非首次公开发行的市场化结果。在确定股权价值并将其分配至各类别证券后，再应用缺乏流动性折扣（"DLOM"）以得出我们普通股的公允价值。应用 DLOM 的理论依据是，作为私营公司股票的所有者，股东出售该股票的机会有限，且任何此类出售都会涉及重大交易成本，从而降低整体公允市场价值。

paras.en: In addition, we also considered any secondary transactions involving our capital stock. In our evaluation of those transactions, we considered the facts and circumstances of each transaction to determine the extent to which they represented a fair value exchange. Factors considered included transaction volume, timing, whether the transactions occurred among unrelated parties, and whether the transactions involved investors with access to our financial information.
paras.zh: 此外，我们还考虑了涉及我们股本的任何二级交易。在评估这些交易时，我们考虑了每项交易的事实和情况，以确定其在多大程度上代表了公允价值交换。考虑的因素包括交易量、时机、交易是否发生在无关联方之间，以及交易是否涉及能够获取我们财务信息的投资者。

paras.en: Application of these approaches involves the use of estimates, judgment, and assumptions that are highly complex and subjective, such as those regarding our expected future revenue, expenses, and future cash flows, discount rates, market multiples, the selection of comparable companies, and the probability of possible future events. Changes in any or all of these estimates and assumptions or the relationships between those assumptions impact our valuations as of each valuation date and may have a material impact on the valuation of our common stock.
paras.zh: 应用这些方法涉及使用高度复杂且主观的估计、判断和假设，例如关于我们预期未来收入、费用和未来现金流量、折现率、市场倍数、可比公司的选择以及可能的未来事件概率的估计、判断和假设。任何或所有这些估计和假设的变化，或这些假设之间关系的变化，都会影响我们在每个估值日的估值，并可能对我们普通股的估值产生重大影响。

paras.en: For valuations after the completion of this offering, our board of directors will determine the fair value of each share of underlying common stock based on the closing price of our common stock as reported on the grant date. Future expense amounts for any particular period could be affected by changes in our assumptions or market conditions.
paras.zh: 对于本次发行完成后的估值，我们的董事会将根据授予日报告的我们普通股收盘价确定每股基础普通股的公允价值。任何特定期间的未来费用金额可能会受到我们假设或市场状况变化的影响。

paras.en: We are an emerging growth company, as defined in the JOBS Act, and, for so long as we continue to be an emerging growth company, we may take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements that would have been applicable were we a public company that was not an emerging growth company. Such exemptions include, but are not limited to, the exemption to comply with the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in our periodic reports and proxy statements, the exemption from holding a non-binding advisory vote on executive compensation, and the exemption from stockholder approval of any golden parachute payments not previously approved. In addition, pursuant to Section 107 of the JOBS Act, as an emerging growth company, we have elected to take advantage of the extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards until those standards would otherwise apply to private companies. If we cease to be an emerging growth company, we will no longer be able to take advantage of these exemptions or the extended transition period for complying with new or revised accounting standards.
paras.zh: 我们是一家《JOBS 法案》所定义的新兴成长型公司，并且只要继续作为新兴成长型公司，我们就可以利用某些豁免，免于遵守若我们是一家非新兴成长型上市公众公司本应适用的各项报告要求。此类豁免包括但不限于：豁免遵守《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》第 404 条的审计师鉴证要求、减少我们定期报告和委托书声明中有关高管薪酬的披露义务、豁免就高管薪酬举行不具约束力的咨询性投票，以及豁免就此前未经批准的任何黄金降落伞付款寻求股东批准。此外，根据《JOBS 法案》第 107 条，作为新兴成长型公司，我们已选择利用延长的过渡期来遵守新的或经修订的会计准则，直至这些准则原本应适用于私营公司之时。如果我们不再是新兴成长型公司，我们将不再能够利用这些豁免或遵守新的或经修订的会计准则的延长过渡期。

paras.en: Refer to Note 3 to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus for further discussion.
paras.zh: 请参阅本招股说明书其他部分所载经审计合并财务报表附注 3 以获取进一步讨论。

paras.en: We are building the fastest AI infrastructure in the world.
paras.zh: 我们正在打造世界上速度最快的 AI 基础设施。

paras.en: In AI, speed is critical to win. Speed improves user engagement, expands product capabilities, can lower operating costs, and opens new markets. It shortens iteration cycles for engineers, researchers, and professionals across industries, allowing them to be more productive. Speed unlocks new applications and new industries.
paras.zh: 在 AI 领域，速度是制胜的关键。速度可提升用户参与度、扩展产品能力、降低运营成本，并开辟新市场。它缩短了各行业工程师、研究人员和专业人士的迭代周期，使他们能够更高效地工作。速度释放了新的应用和新的行业。

paras.en: In technology, “speed unlocking value” is a pattern that has repeated itself over the past 30 years. Faster solutions are used more often and for more demanding tasks. For example, the speed of broadband transformed the internet from static pages into real-time applications, enabling new products and industries. Similarly, in search, Google showed that even short delays in delivering answers significantly reduced usage and engagement.
paras.zh: 在技术领域，“速度释放价值”是过去 30 年间不断重演的模式。更快的解决方案被更频繁地使用，并用于更严苛的任务。例如，宽带的速度将互联网从静态页面转变为实时应用，催生了新产品和新行业。同样，在搜索领域，Google 表明，即使交付答案出现短暂延迟，也会显著降低使用量和参与度。

paras.en: AI repeats this pattern. As AI has moved from novelty to necessity, AI work has grown more demanding, and speed has become a bottleneck. Faster AI does more work in less time, providing better answers sooner.
paras.zh: AI 重复着这一模式。随着 AI 从新奇事物变为必需品，AI 工作负载日益严苛，速度已成为瓶颈。更快的 AI 能在更短时间内完成更多工作，更快地提供更好的答案。

paras.en: Our solutions are built for speed. Cerebras Inference delivers answers up to 15 times faster than leading GPU-based solutions as benchmarked on leading open-source models. Similarly, many customers have achieved more than 10 times faster training time-to-solution compared to leading GPU systems of the same generation.
paras.zh: 我们的解决方案专为速度而构建。在领先的开源模型基准测试中，Cerebras Inference 交付答案的速度最高可达领先的基于 GPU 的解决方案的 15 倍。同样，许多客户相比同代领先的 GPU 系统，实现了超过 10 倍的训练求解时间提速。

paras.en: These performance breakthroughs are the result of our core innovation: the world’s first and only commercialized wafer-scale processor. Called the Wafer-Scale Engine (“WSE”), our processor is 58 times larger than NVIDIA’s B200 chip and has 2,625 times more memory bandwidth than NVIDIA’s B200 package, which contains two individual chips. To build the WSE, we solved the 75-year-old compute industry problem of wafer-scale integration to produce, yield, power, and cool a chip of this size. This size is what enables our incredible AI speeds. By bringing massive compute and memory onto a single piece of silicon and integrating it into a purpose-built system and software stack, we deliver exceptional AI speed for customers on premises and via the cloud.
paras.zh: 这些性能突破源于我们的核心创新：世界上首个也是唯一一个商业化的晶圆级处理器。我们的处理器名为晶圆级引擎（"WSE"），其尺寸是 NVIDIA B200 芯片的 58 倍，内存带宽是包含两颗独立芯片的 NVIDIA B200 封装体的 2,625 倍。为打造 WSE，我们解决了计算行业存在 75 年之久的晶圆级集成难题，实现了这一尺寸芯片的生产、良率、供电和散热。正是这一尺寸成就了我们惊人的 AI 速度。通过将大规模算力和内存集成到单块硅片上，并将其整合进专为特定目的打造的系统与软件栈，我们为本地部署和云端客户提供卓越的 AI 速度。

paras.en: Our strategic partners and customers include hyperscalers, foundation model labs, AI-native and digital-native businesses, enterprises, and Sovereign AI initiatives. OpenAI, the world’s leading foundation model lab, selected us to be its fast inference solution. With Cerebras, OpenAI’s Codex-Spark users turn ideas into working software in seconds. This partnership is an example of tight hardware-software co-design with a leading frontier model lab. AWS, the world’s leading hyperscale cloud, has signed a binding term sheet with us to become the first hyperscaler to deploy Cerebras in its own data centers, providing massive distribution to a broad base of enterprise customers.
paras.zh: 我们的战略合作伙伴和客户包括超大规模云服务商、基础模型实验室、AI 原生和数字原生企业、大型企业以及主权 AI 计划。全球领先的基础模型实验室 OpenAI 选择我们作为其快速推理解决方案。借助 Cerebras,OpenAI 的 Codex-Spark 用户可在数秒内将想法转化为可运行的软件。这一合作是与领先前沿模型实验室进行紧密软硬件协同设计的典范。全球领先的超大规模云服务商 AWS 已与我们签署具有约束力的条款清单，将成为首家在自有数据中心部署 Cerebras 的超大规模云服务商，为广泛的企业客户群体提供大规模分销渠道。

paras.en: Our customers use Cerebras solutions to run applications that demand speed, scale, and intelligence. This work includes training and serving large frontier models with near-instant responses, processing massive datasets in real time, and generating full-stack applications in a single step. Once customers adopt fast inference, user expectations for interactivity rise, and engineering teams shift from latency optimizations to other work, making it difficult to return to slower inference.
paras.zh: 我们的客户使用 Cerebras 解决方案运行对速度、规模和智能有要求的应用。这些工作包括以近乎即时的响应训练和提供大型前沿模型服务、实时处理海量数据集，以及一步生成全栈应用。一旦客户采用快速推理，用户对交互性的期望就会提高，工程团队也会从延迟优化转向其他工作，从而难以再回到较慢的推理。

paras.en: We deliver our solutions to customers in several different ways. Organizations that require full data and infrastructure control can purchase Cerebras AI supercomputers for on-premises deployments. Customers seeking cloud flexibility can access Cerebras compute through consumption-based models on Cerebras Cloud or through partner clouds. For example, our high-speed inference services are available through partners, including AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Marketplace, IBM watsonx Model Gateway, Vercel AI Gateway, OpenRouter, and Hugging Face, enabling seamless adoption within existing workflows.
paras.zh: 我们通过多种不同方式向客户交付解决方案。需要完全掌控数据和基础设施的组织可以购买 Cerebras AI 超级计算机进行本地部署。寻求云灵活性的客户可以通过 Cerebras Cloud 上基于用量的模式或通过合作伙伴云获取 Cerebras 算力。例如，我们的高速推理服务可通过合作伙伴获取，包括 AWS Marketplace、Microsoft Marketplace、IBM watsonx Model Gateway、Vercel AI Gateway、OpenRouter 和 Hugging Face，从而能够在现有工作流中无缝采用。

paras.en: Our ability to deliver differentiated performance has made us a strategic partner to many of our largest customers. Beyond providing compute infrastructure, we provide AI services to our customers to co-develop solutions to address their most complex challenges, from training state-of-the-art models to optimizing deployments for each application’s needs. These partnerships have expanded over time; notably, our top ten customers by year-to-date revenue through December 31, 2025 increased their aggregate spend with us by approximately 80% within 12 months of their initial purchase, often including contracts for co-development.
paras.zh: 我们提供差异化性能的能力使我们成为许多最大客户的战略合作伙伴。除提供算力基础设施外，我们还向客户提供 AI 服务，共同开发解决方案以应对其最复杂的挑战，从训练最先进的模型到针对每个应用的需求优化部署。这些合作关系随时间不断扩大；值得注意的是，按截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年初至今收入计算，我们的前十大客户在首次购买后的 12 个月内将其与我们的总支出增加了约 80%，其中往往包括共同开发合同。

paras.en: AI is one of the fastest growing technologies in history. We believe that our high-speed AI solutions give us a meaningful competitive advantage in this market. We believe that further adoption of AI, accelerated by increased penetration, more frequent usage, and more complex applications, will continue to rapidly expand the market. According to IDC, investments in AI solutions and services are projected to yield a global cumulative impact of $22.3 trillion by 2030, representing approximately 3.7% of the global GDP. The combined market for AI training infrastructure and our addressable market within AI inference is estimated to be $251 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow to $672 billion by 2029—a 28% CAGR, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. This estimate indicates that AI inference will grow more than twice as fast as AI training infrastructure through 2029. With the fastest inference platform on the market, as benchmarked by Artificial Analysis, and a proven track record in large-scale training, we believe we are well-positioned to capture growth across both parts of the AI infrastructure market.
paras.zh: AI 是历史上增长最快的技术之一。我们相信，我们的高速 AI 解决方案使我们在这一市场中拥有显著的竞争优势。我们相信，随着渗透率提升、使用频率增加以及应用日益复杂，AI 的进一步普及将加速，并持续推动市场快速扩张。根据 IDC 的数据，到 2030 年，AI 解决方案与服务的投资预计将在全球产生累计 $22.3 trillion 的影响，约占全球 GDP 的 3.7%。根据 Bloomberg Intelligence 的数据，AI 训练基础设施市场与我们在 AI 推理领域的可服务市场合计规模在 2025 年估计为 $251 billion，并预计到 2029 年增长至 $672 billion——年复合增长率（CAGR）为 28%。该估计表明，到 2029 年，AI 推理的增长速度将超过 AI 训练基础设施的两倍以上。凭借以 Artificial Analysis 为基准的市场上最快的推理平台，以及在大规模训练方面经过验证的过往业绩，我们相信我们处于有利位置，能够把握 AI 基础设施市场两部分的增长机遇。

paras.en: Our growth reflects the broader acceleration of AI adoption. Our revenue increased from $24.6 million in 2022 to $78.7 million in 2023 and to $290.3 million in 2024, representing a more than tenfold increase over three years. Our revenue increased to $510.0 million in 2025, representing year-over-year growth of 76%. We earned net income of $237.8 million in 2025 and incurred net loss of $481.6 million in 2024. Our gross margin was 12%, 33%, 42%, and 39% in 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. We incurred non-GAAP net loss of $75.7 million in 2025 and $21.8 million in 2024, after excluding the impact of stock-based compensation expense and change in fair value (extinguishment) of forward contract liability from our GAAP net income (loss). For more information and for a reconciliation of non-GAAP net loss to net income (loss), see the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Non-GAAP Financial Measures.”
paras.zh: 我们的增长反映了 AI 采用的更广泛加速。我们的收入从 2022 年的 $24.6 million 增至 2023 年的 $78.7 million，并进一步增至 2024 年的 $290.3 million，三年间增长超过十倍。我们的收入在 2025 年增至 $510.0 million，同比增长 76%。我们在 2025 年实现净利润 $237.8 million，并在 2024 年产生净亏损 $481.6 million。我们的毛利率在 2022 年、2023 年、2024 年和 2025 年分别为 12%、33%、42% 和 39%。在从我们的 GAAP 净利润（亏损）中剔除股权激励费用以及远期合同负债公允价值变动（清偿）的影响后，我们在 2025 年产生非 GAAP 净亏损 $75.7 million，在 2024 年产生非 GAAP 净亏损 $21.8 million。有关更多信息以及非 GAAP 净亏损与净利润（亏损）的对账，请参见标题为“管理层对财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析——非 GAAP 财务指标”的章节。

paras.en: #### AI is the Next Technological Shift
paras.zh: #### AI 是下一次技术变革

paras.en: Over the past 50 years, the compute industry has undergone a series of secular shifts, each of which expanded access to compute and transformed global productivity. In the 1990s, the Internet reshaped how people worked, communicated, transacted, and learned, catalyzing new industries and business models. In the 2000s and 2010s, the proliferation of mobile devices and the emergence of cloud computing delivered unprecedented flexibility, scale, and reach, supporting million s of new digital products and experiences.
paras.zh: 在过去 50 年里，算力行业经历了一系列长期性变革，每一次变革都扩大了算力的可及性，并重塑了全球生产力。20 世纪 90 年代，互联网重塑了人们工作、沟通、交易和学习的方式，催生了新的行业和商业模式。21 世纪头十年和 2010 年代，移动设备的普及和云计算的兴起带来了前所未有的灵活性、规模和覆盖范围，支撑了数以百万计的新数字产品和体验。

paras.en: We believe AI represents the next major technological shift—one with the potential to exceed the transformational impact of prior cycles.
paras.zh: 我们认为，AI 代表着下一次重大技术变革——其变革性影响有可能超过以往各轮周期。

paras.en: In comparison to previous technology shifts, the adoption of AI is astonishing. Its market penetration has occurred multiple times faster than the PC and the cloud. ChatGPT reached 100 million users in less than 2.5 months, more than twenty times faster than Facebook. As of September 2025, ChatGPT reported 700 million weekly active users.
paras.zh: 与以往的技术变革相比，AI 的采用速度令人惊叹。其市场渗透速度比 PC 和云快数倍。ChatGPT 在不到 2.5 个月内就达到了 1 亿用户，比 Facebook 快二十多倍。截至 2025 年 9 月，ChatGPT 报告拥有 7 亿周活跃用户。

paras.en: Number of Years to 100 Million Users* ChatGPT Instagram Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Netflix 100 Million Users 0 Users Number of Users The time at which a platform achieved 100 million users is based on each platform’s reporting. The definitions differ across platforms (e.g., ‘‘Active Users.” MAUs. etc.), and even similarly titled metrics are not directly comparable across platforms. The slopes of the lines are illustrative. Netflix reflects Netflix streaming subscribers.
paras.zh: 达到 1 亿用户所需年数* ChatGPT Instagram Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Netflix 1 亿用户 0 用户 用户数量 平台达到 1 亿用户的时间基于各平台自身的报告。各平台的定义不同（例如“活跃用户”、MAU 等），即便是名称相似的指标，在不同平台之间也不可直接比较。各线条的斜率为示意性。Netflix 反映的是 Netflix 流媒体订阅用户数。

paras.en: According to Pew Research Center, as of June 2025, around 62% of U.S. adults interacted with AI at least several times a week, with 31% doing so almost constantly (at least several times a day), and one-third of U.S. adults under 30 saying they interacted with AI several times a day. Additionally, the Digital Education Council found in 2024 that 86% of higher-education students used AI. According to a McKinsey survey in 2025, the share of respondents saying their organizations are using AI in at least one business function has increased since their research last year: 88% reported regular AI use in at least one business function in 2025 compared with 78% a year ago. In the third quarter of 2025, Gallup reported daily use of AI in the workplace had more than doubled in the past 12 months, with 10% of U.S. employees reporting they used AI in their daily roles.
paras.zh: 根据皮尤研究中心的数据，截至 2025 年 6 月，约 62% 的美国成年人每周至少数次与 AI 互动，其中 31% 几乎持续使用（每天至少数次），而 30 岁以下的美国成年人中有三分之一表示他们每天数次与 AI 互动。此外，数字教育委员会在 2024 年发现，86% 的高等教育学生使用 AI。根据麦肯锡 2025 年的一项调查，表示其组织在至少一项业务职能中使用 AI 的受访者比例较其去年研究有所上升：2025 年有 88% 的受访者报告在至少一项业务职能中定期使用 AI，而一年前为 78%。2025 年第三季度，盖洛普报告称，工作场所中 AI 的日常使用在过去 12 个月中增长了一倍以上，10% 的美国员工表示他们在日常工作中使用 AI。

paras.en: The strong rate of AI adoption is driven by the simple fact that AI has transitioned from novelty to necessity and is now used across consumer and enterprise domains. Individuals and organizations rely on AI to solve problems, build products, accelerate research, improve patient outcomes, enhance decision-making, streamline operations, enable innovation, and deliver personalized experiences.
paras.zh: AI 采用率之所以强劲，原因很简单：AI 已从新奇事物转变为必需品，如今在消费者和企业领域得到广泛使用。个人和组织依赖 AI 来解决问题、构建产品、加速研究、改善患者治疗效果、增强决策、简化运营、推动创新并提供个性化体验。

paras.en: The rise of AI depends on massive computational resources. This is where Cerebras fits in.
paras.zh: AI 的崛起依赖于海量计算资源。这正是 Cerebras 的用武之地。

paras.zh: 算力周期演变——1980 年代至 2030 年代 1,000,000 10,000 100 微型计算机 PC AI 时代 移动互联网 桌面互联网 百万台 按对数刻度绘制 预计 10B+ 5B+ 1.5B+ 500M+ 1 10M+ 0 1980 1990 2000 2010 2020 2030

paras.en: **Inference is Driving the AI Compute Demand, as Frontier AI Models Grow More Capable**
paras.zh: **随着前沿 AI 模型能力不断增强，推理正在推动 AI 算力需求**

paras.en: AI is composed of two stages: training and inference. Training is the process of creating and teaching the AI model; inference is the process of using the model to generate responses. Early progress in AI came primarily from training larger models. Larger models, which used more compute during training, improved AI’s accuracy. In this training-centric era, inference was straightforward and required little computation; it simply generated answers from a trained model in a single step.
paras.zh: AI 由两个阶段构成：训练与推理。训练是创建并教导 AI 模型的过程；推理是使用模型生成回答的过程。AI 早期的进展主要来自训练更大的模型。更大的模型在训练时使用更多算力，从而提升了 AI 的准确度。在这个以训练为中心的时代，推理简单直接、所需计算很少；它只是从已训练的模型中一步生成答案。

paras.en: Today, AI has entered a new era centered on inference. New techniques have emerged that make models smarter as they are being used. This approach—called “inference-time compute” or “test-time compute”—has become the dominant mode of inference.
paras.zh: 如今，AI 已进入一个以推理为中心的新时代。新技术的出现使模型在被使用的过程中变得更智能。这种方法被称为“推理时算力”或“测试时算力”，已成为推理的主导模式。

paras.en: We Are in the Age of Reasoning Inference Time Compute Model Intelligence Inference Time Scaling Pre-training Scaling GPT-3 GPT-4 GPT-5
paras.zh: 我们正处于推理时代 推理时算力 模型智能 推理时扩展 预训练扩展 GPT-3 GPT-4 GPT-5

paras.en: Instead of depending primarily on the trained model for accuracy, today’s frontier models—such as OpenAI’s GPT-5.4, Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7, and Google’s Gemini 3.1 Pro—perform substantial computation during inference to simulate reasoning. These models effectively “think through” the problem: planning steps, checking their own work, and refining responses before delivering a final, higher-quality result. These additional steps use substantially more compute during inference, while producing more accurate answers.
paras.zh: 如今的前沿模型——例如 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.4、Anthropic 的 Claude Opus 4.7 和 Google 的 Gemini 3.1 Pro——不再主要依赖已训练的模型来保证准确度，而是在推理期间执行大量计算以模拟推理过程。这些模型实际上会“思考”问题：规划步骤、检查自身工作，并在给出最终更高质量结果之前完善回答。这些额外步骤在推理期间使用显著更多的算力，同时产生更准确的答案。

paras.en: These reasoning capabilities have fundamentally changed how people use AI. Inference is no longer limited to answering questions; modern AI applications now perform actions on behalf of their users. They can directly book travel itineraries, code full web applications from scratch, help customers apply for mortgages, automatically analyze legal contracts for discrepancies, process insurance claims, and more. As a result, demand for AI inference has surged alongside the adoption of these smarter reasoning models that leverage more inference-time compute.
paras.zh: 这些推理能力从根本上改变了人们使用 AI 的方式。推理不再局限于回答问题；现代 AI 应用如今可代表用户执行操作。它们可以直接预订旅行行程、从零编写完整的 Web 应用、帮助客户申请抵押贷款、自动分析法律合同中的不一致之处、处理保险理赔等等。因此，随着这些利用更多推理时算力的更智能推理模型得到采用，对 AI 推理的需求也随之激增。

paras.en: Ultimately, inference compute demand is driven by the compounding effect of three forces: the number of users, the frequency of use, and the compute per use. Each of these forces is growing at an extraordinary rate, producing a geometric expansion of demand for inference and its underlying compute.
paras.zh: 归根结底，推理算力需求由三股力量的复合效应驱动：用户数量、使用频率以及每次使用的算力。这三股力量均以惊人的速度增长，推动推理及其底层算力的需求呈几何级数扩张。

paras.en: Reasoning during inference delivers smarter AI responses but requires significantly more compute. As models become more capable, users rely on them for increasingly ambitious tasks, further driving compute needs. Today’s workloads—including video generation, deep research, and long-form analysis—can require many orders of magnitude more compute than answering basic questions.
paras.zh: 推理过程能够带来更智能的 AI 响应，但需要显著更多的算力。随着模型能力不断增强，用户会依赖它们完成越来越宏大的任务，从而进一步推高算力需求。如今的工作负载——包括视频生成、深度研究和长篇分析——所需的算力可能比回答基础问题高出许多个数量级。

paras.en: #### Reasoning Makes Inference Speed a Necessity
paras.zh: #### 推理使推理速度成为必需

paras.en: Speed enables reasoning models to deliver more accurate answers faster, reducing the frustration created by forcing customers to wait for answers.
paras.zh: 速度使推理模型能够更快地给出更准确的答案，减少因让客户等待答案而产生的挫败感。

paras.en: Reasoning changes the shape of inference. Reasoning systems do not complete tasks in a single request-and-response step. They execute a sequence of sequential and dependent steps—such as planning, refinement, and verification—until the task is completed. Each step consumes compute and contributes to total completion time. Slower execution of each step compounds, and then the task takes much longer to complete. Faster execution at each step shortens the overall time to answer.
paras.zh: 推理改变了推理的形态。推理系统并非在单次请求—响应步骤中完成任务。它们会执行一系列顺序且相互依赖的步骤——例如规划、细化和验证——直至任务完成。每一步都会消耗算力，并计入总完成时间。每一步执行得越慢，其影响会层层叠加，任务完成所需时间便会大幅延长。每一步执行得越快，回答所需的整体时间就越短。

paras.en: Complex tasks (harder problems) are more valuable to solve but they require the reasoning system to go through a longer sequence of steps. This amplifies the benefit of speed and the penalty for being slow. Speed enables more accurate answers to harder problems in less time. Speed expands the range of tasks that AI can address, thereby broadening its addressable market. Conversely, slow AI produces longer wait times, making many applications impractical to deploy.
paras.zh: 复杂任务（更难的问题）解决起来更有价值，但它们要求推理系统经历更长的步骤序列。这放大了速度带来的收益，也放大了缓慢带来的代价。速度使更难的问题能够在更短时间内得到更准确的答案。速度拓展了 AI 可处理的任务范围，从而拓宽了其可服务市场。反之，缓慢的 AI 会造成更长的等待时间，使许多应用无法实际部署。
